tuples.episode_object: a stack of split oak staves seasoning in the open beside a cooperage
tuples.time_place_scope: a forest district of central France in the working years of the 1800s
tuples.mechanism: the forest a stave comes from changes what a spirit becomes, so cask making ties distilling to distant woodland management
tuples.evidence_lens: forest management records and the cooperage purchase accounts for oak staves

tuples.episode_object: a bottle labelled with a stated year drawn from a single cellar lot
tuples.time_place_scope: a merchant bottling room in western France in the 1800s
tuples.mechanism: a claim of vintage requires records that can be checked, so paperwork rather than taste becomes the guarantee of an age
tuples.evidence_lens: cellar stock books and the trade rules governing statements of vintage and age

tuples.episode_object: a tasting bench of small glasses drawn from casks of many ages
tuples.time_place_scope: a blending cellar in western France in the 1900s, where casks of many ages were married for a house style
tuples.mechanism: a house style is made by marrying many ages, so continuity rests on a library of old casks rather than on any recipe
tuples.evidence_lens: cellar inventories of reserve stock and the blending records of trading houses

tuples.episode_object: a small still mounted on a cart moving between farms in winter
tuples.time_place_scope: a rural district of eastern France in the distilling season of the 1800s
tuples.mechanism: an itinerant still lets smallholders distil their own fruit under supervision, and that right is customary and jealously kept
tuples.evidence_lens: excise registers of travelling stills and the commune records of distilling rights

tuples.episode_object: a shipping case marked for a colonial garrison mess
tuples.time_place_scope: a French port loading for overseas territories in the 1880s
tuples.mechanism: empire creates a captive market, and export volumes rather than home demand carry a district through its poorer decades
tuples.evidence_lens: export shipping manifests and the colonial commissariat purchase records

tuples.episode_object: a measured addition of grape spirit run into a cask of sweet wine
tuples.time_place_scope: an Iberian wine lodge in the shipping seasons of the 1700s
tuples.mechanism: distilled spirit is used to stabilise and sweeten wine, so brandy making is tied to a wine trade it does not itself supply
tuples.evidence_lens: lodge production accounts and the export declarations filed for fortified wines

tuples.episode_object: a seized bottle found coloured with caramel and thinned with weak spirit
tuples.time_place_scope: a French market town in the 1900s, where caramel-coloured bottles were sampled by inspectors
tuples.mechanism: colour is read as age, so colour is added, and the law responds by defining which additions may be made and declared
tuples.evidence_lens: public analyst reports and the regulations defining permitted additions to spirits

tuples.episode_object: a price list setting out grades by the youngest cask in each blend
tuples.time_place_scope: a merchant office in western France in the 1900s
tuples.mechanism: age claims are standardised on the youngest component, and a shared counting rule makes competing grades comparable
tuples.evidence_lens: trade association rules and the merchants' printed grade and price lists

tuples.episode_object: a still charged with pressed grape skins swept from a wine press
tuples.time_place_scope: a north Italian farm still house at the end of vintage in the 1800s
tuples.mechanism: the pressed residue of wine making holds enough sugar to distil, so a careful farm throws nothing of the vintage away
tuples.evidence_lens: farm accounts and the agricultural manuals describing the use of pressing waste

tuples.episode_object: a commune register listing households permitted to distil their own fruit
tuples.time_place_scope: a French rural commune in the 1900s, where household fruit distilling was entered in a commune register
tuples.mechanism: a household right to distil a fixed quantity survives as a privilege, and the register is where that custom is written down
tuples.evidence_lens: commune distilling registers and the revenue rules limiting household allowances

tuples.episode_object: a herbal page describing wormwood as a bitter tonic for the stomach
tuples.time_place_scope: a European printing town in the herbal decades of the 1500s
tuples.mechanism: wormwood enters the record as a medicinal bitter, and the plant is written about for centuries before any famous drink exists
tuples.evidence_lens: printed herbals and the apothecary registers listing wormwood preparations

tuples.episode_object: a farm still in a high valley charged with local wormwood and anise
tuples.time_place_scope: a Swiss Jura valley in the working winters of the 1790s
tuples.mechanism: an upland district with herbs and a still makes a regional remedy, and the drink starts as a rural preparation sold by the flask
tuples.evidence_lens: commune distilling registers and the regional accounts of herb gathering

tuples.episode_object: a maceration tun where dried herbs steep in spirit before a second run
tuples.time_place_scope: a Jura distillery in the working season of the 1800s
tuples.mechanism: steeping and then distilling extracts aroma without bitterness, and the order of those two steps decides the finished character
tuples.evidence_lens: distillery recipe books and the technical manuals written for herb distillers

tuples.episode_object: a colouring vat where fresh herbs steep until the spirit turns green
tuples.time_place_scope: a French distillery finishing room in the 1870s
tuples.mechanism: a second steeping of green herbs colours the spirit naturally, and that colour later fades with age into a settled amber
tuples.evidence_lens: distillery process notes and the trade descriptions of colouring practice

tuples.episode_object: a slotted spoon and a dripping water carafe set over a stemmed glass
tuples.time_place_scope: a French cafe terrace in the late afternoons of the 1880s
tuples.mechanism: adding water clouds the drink as its oils leave solution, and the slow preparation becomes the visible part of the custom
tuples.evidence_lens: cafe stock and equipment inventories and the printed guides to cafe service

tuples.episode_object: a field issue flask carried with a garrison ration in a dry climate
tuples.time_place_scope: a French garrison in North Africa in the campaign years of the 1840s
tuples.mechanism: a bitter is issued in the belief that it prevents fever, and army habit carries a regional drink back into metropolitan cities
tuples.evidence_lens: military medical reports and the commissariat records of issued supplies

tuples.episode_object: a marbled table with a printed tariff of drinks by the hour
tuples.time_place_scope: a Paris boulevard cafe in the fashionable evenings of the 1870s
tuples.mechanism: a fixed hour of the day is given over to one drink, and a city routine rather than the drink itself is what spreads the habit
tuples.evidence_lens: cafe licence records, tariff cards, and the journalism and memoirs of the period

tuples.episode_object: a rectifying column supplying cheap industrial spirit to a herb works
tuples.time_place_scope: a French industrial distillery in the expanding decades of the 1880s
tuples.mechanism: cheap base spirit lets a costly herbal preparation be sold at a low price, and volume rather than skill drives the trade
tuples.evidence_lens: distillery output returns and the trade journals reporting on production methods

tuples.episode_object: a seized sample coloured with copper salts instead of with green herbs
tuples.time_place_scope: a French market town in the 1900s, where coloured imitations were sampled for copper salts
tuples.mechanism: cheap imitation is coloured with metal salts, and harm caused by those substitutes is later confused with the drink itself
tuples.evidence_lens: public analyst reports and the prosecution records under adulteration statutes

tuples.episode_object: a price list showing wine dearer than a herbal spirit in one cafe
tuples.time_place_scope: a French provincial town in the vine sickness years of the 1880s
tuples.mechanism: a vine pest raises wine prices, and drinkers move to a cheaper distilled substitute for reasons of household economy
tuples.evidence_lens: cafe price lists and the agricultural inquiry reports on the vine sickness

tuples.episode_object: a clinical case book entry describing a patient in a public hospital
tuples.time_place_scope: a French city hospital in the debating years of the 1860s
tuples.mechanism: a distinct illness is proposed and named, and medical argument rather than measurement shapes what the public comes to believe
tuples.evidence_lens: hospital case books and the medical society papers debating the proposed illness

tuples.episode_object: a printed petition sheet gathering signatures against a herbal spirit
tuples.time_place_scope: a Swiss canton in the 1900s, where petitioners carried a temperance campaign to referendum
tuples.mechanism: a public vote and then a national ban follow a long temperance campaign, so law arrives through petition and referendum
tuples.evidence_lens: petition rolls, referendum results, and the parliamentary debates of the period

tuples.episode_object: a reformulated bottle of anise spirit made without the banned herb
tuples.time_place_scope: a southern French distillery in the reworking years of the 1930s
tuples.mechanism: a ban is met by reformulation, and the substitute style becomes a regional institution of its own within one generation
tuples.evidence_lens: distillery recipe records and the regulations defining permitted formulations

tuples.episode_object: a glass with a bulge blown into the stem marking a single measure
tuples.time_place_scope: a French glassworks and cafe supply store in the 1890s
tuples.mechanism: the vessel itself states the dose, and pricing, taxation, and service all settle around a shape blown into the glass
tuples.evidence_lens: glassworks catalogues and the cafe equipment inventories listing measured glasses

tuples.episode_object: a lump of sugar resting on a pierced spoon above a clouding glass
tuples.time_place_scope: a French provincial cafe in the working evenings of the 1880s
tuples.mechanism: sweetening softens a bitter preparation, and a small utensil trade grows up around one single step of one drink
tuples.evidence_lens: cutlery trade catalogues and the cafe supply invoices surviving from the period

tuples.episode_object: a wage book from a distillery employing much of a small border town
tuples.time_place_scope: a Jura border town in the working years of the 1890s
tuples.mechanism: one product can carry a town's employment, and a later prohibition is felt as an industrial closure before anything else
tuples.evidence_lens: distillery wage books and the municipal records of employment and of relief

tuples.episode_object: a lithographed poster showing a clouded glass and a water carafe
tuples.time_place_scope: a French printing shop in the advertising years of the 1890s
tuples.mechanism: colour printing makes a drink visible in the street, and imagery rather than description carries a product into new markets
tuples.evidence_lens: print shop order books and the surviving poster collections held in public archives

tuples.episode_object: a crate of bottles carried across a mountain border by night
tuples.time_place_scope: a Swiss and French frontier in the years after the ban in the 1910s
tuples.mechanism: prohibition in one country and not another creates a border trade, and enforcement records become the only production figures
tuples.evidence_lens: customs seizure records and the frontier court proceedings of the period

tuples.episode_object: a laboratory flask of distilled sample measured for its herb compounds
tuples.time_place_scope: a European analytical laboratory in the re-examining years of the 1990s
tuples.mechanism: later chemical measurement finds far less of the suspected compound than assumed, and an old alarm is quietly revised
tuples.evidence_lens: published analytical studies and the archived samples held for laboratory testing

tuples.episode_object: a regulation sheet setting a permitted limit for a named compound
tuples.time_place_scope: a European regulatory office in the revising years of the 1990s
tuples.mechanism: a numeric limit replaces an outright ban, and a drink returns to legal sale defined by a threshold rather than by its name
tuples.evidence_lens: published regulations and the technical committee papers setting compound limits

tuples.episode_object: a lemon tree wintered under a sloped glass roof beside a garden wall
tuples.time_place_scope: a north European estate orangery through the cold months of the 1600s
tuples.mechanism: a warm-climate fruit is grown out of climate under glass, and the cost of heating decides who may drink a fresh fruit drink
tuples.evidence_lens: estate garden accounts and the printed treatises on orangery construction

tuples.episode_object: a crate of paper-wrapped lemons packed in a hold with dry straw
tuples.time_place_scope: a passage from a Sicilian port toward northern Europe in the 1700s
tuples.mechanism: citrus rots quickly, so wrapping, stowage, and sailing dates set which northern markets can be reached with sound fruit
tuples.evidence_lens: ship cargo manifests and the port arrival records noting condition on landing

tuples.episode_object: a brass tank strapped to a vendor's back with a tap at the hip
tuples.time_place_scope: a Paris street in the trading summers of the 1700s
tuples.mechanism: a licensed body of sellers holds the right to make and hawk the drink, so a guild rather than a shop controls a street trade
tuples.evidence_lens: guild statutes of the drink sellers and the municipal registers of licensed vendors

tuples.episode_object: a loaf of refined sugar cut with iron nippers into a mixing bowl
tuples.time_place_scope: a household still room in southern England in the 1700s
tuples.mechanism: the sweetness depends on a colonial plantation crop, so a simple fruit drink sits at the end of a long and coerced supply chain
tuples.evidence_lens: household account books and the grocers' import and price records for sugar

tuples.episode_object: a ship's daily issue of lemon juice measured out into a mess kid
tuples.time_place_scope: a long naval voyage from a British port in the 1790s
tuples.mechanism: citrus is issued against scurvy, and a medical finding turns a pleasant drink into a compulsory item of ship's provisioning
tuples.evidence_lens: naval medical reports and the victualling records of citrus issued to crews

tuples.episode_object: a straw-packed ice chest under the counter of a summer refreshment stall
tuples.time_place_scope: an American east coast city in the hot months of the 1830s
tuples.mechanism: cut winter ice shipped and stored lets cold drinks be sold in summer, so refrigeration creates the trade rather than the recipe
tuples.evidence_lens: ice company delivery books and the refreshment stall licence records

tuples.episode_object: a stoppered bottle of thick lemon syrup kept in a cool larder
tuples.time_place_scope: an English country household in the preserving weeks of the 1800s
tuples.mechanism: heavy sugar preserves the juice out of season, so a syrup rather than the fruit is what a household actually stores
tuples.evidence_lens: household receipt manuscripts and the still room books kept by mistresses of houses

tuples.episode_object: a lead-chambered gas apparatus charging a tank of sweetened lemon water
tuples.time_place_scope: a mineral water works in a British city in the 1830s
tuples.mechanism: carbonating a fruit drink makes it keep and sparkle, and a chemical apparatus turns a kitchen preparation into a factory good
tuples.evidence_lens: manufacturers' plant descriptions and the trade journals on aerated water works

tuples.episode_object: a glass bottle with a pinched neck holding a marble against the gas
tuples.time_place_scope: an English bottling works in the working weeks of the 1870s
tuples.mechanism: gas pressure needs a closure that reseals, and bottle design rather than the drink becomes the industry's technical problem
tuples.evidence_lens: glassworks catalogues and the bottling works production and returns records

tuples.episode_object: a seized sample found soured with mineral acid and sweetened with lead
tuples.time_place_scope: a British market town in the inspecting years of the 1850s
tuples.mechanism: cheap acids imitate fruit and cheap salts sweeten, so public analysis becomes the only defence an ordinary buyer has
tuples.evidence_lens: public analyst reports and the prosecution records under food adulteration law

tuples.episode_object: a temperance hall counter selling bottled fruit drinks after a meeting
tuples.time_place_scope: an English industrial town in the campaigning years of the 1850s
tuples.mechanism: abstinence societies need an alternative to sell, and a soft drink trade grows out of a moral campaign as much as a thirst
tuples.evidence_lens: temperance society minute books and the accounts of hall refreshment sales

tuples.episode_object: a printed shop card distinguishing a fruit squash from a ready drink
tuples.time_place_scope: a British grocery in the 1900s, where labels distinguished fruit squash from ready drinks
tuples.mechanism: names are given legal meanings so a buyer knows the fruit content, and a familiar word becomes a regulated description
tuples.evidence_lens: trade circulars and the composition standards published for fruit drinks

tuples.episode_object: a marble counter with syrup pumps and a nickel-plated draught arm
tuples.time_place_scope: an American drug store in the working afternoons of the 1890s
tuples.mechanism: a pharmacy counter becomes a place of refreshment, and the shop fitting itself creates a new habit of sitting and drinking
tuples.evidence_lens: drug store equipment catalogues and the shop day books of counter sales

tuples.episode_object: a canvas booth of glass jars and cut lemons at a fairground gate
tuples.time_place_scope: an American county fair in the summer weeks of the 1880s
tuples.mechanism: the drink is made in front of the buyer at a temporary stall, and seasonal fairs rather than shops carry it into rural districts
tuples.evidence_lens: fair association accounts and the stall rental records of agricultural shows

tuples.episode_object: a factory vat where lemon juice is precipitated with lime for its acid
tuples.time_place_scope: a Sicilian citrus works in the manufacturing decades of the 1800s
tuples.mechanism: citric acid is extracted from the fruit as an industrial chemical, and the drink's key taste becomes a purchasable powder
tuples.evidence_lens: works production records and the chemical trade journals describing the process

tuples.episode_object: a tray of candied peel drying beside a room of squeezed lemon halves
tuples.time_place_scope: a southern Italian preserving workshop in the 1800s
tuples.mechanism: the skin is worth more than the juice in some seasons, so which part counts as the by-product depends on that year's market
tuples.evidence_lens: workshop account books and the export records of preserved and candied peel

tuples.episode_object: a handwritten receipt for lemon water scented with a little ambergris
tuples.time_place_scope: an English gentlewoman's still room in the 1600s
tuples.mechanism: drink recipes circulate in manuscript between households, so the receipt book is how a domestic technology is actually passed on
tuples.evidence_lens: household receipt manuscripts and the family papers in which they are preserved

tuples.episode_object: an earthen pot of lime water with salt and cumin sold from a barrow
tuples.time_place_scope: a north Indian market street in the hot season of the 1800s
tuples.mechanism: a cooling drink is adapted to local fruit and salt for heat and thirst, so one idea takes a different shape in each climate
tuples.evidence_lens: travellers' accounts and the municipal records licensing street refreshment sellers

tuples.episode_object: a filling line of returnable bottles capped with crimped metal crowns
tuples.time_place_scope: a bottling works in a north American city in the 1900s
tuples.mechanism: a cheap disposable seal makes high-speed filling possible, and delivery by lorry and crate replaces sale from an open tank
tuples.evidence_lens: bottling works production records and the trade catalogues of capping machinery

tuples.episode_object: a ration-period bottle labelled as a lemon-flavoured drink without fruit
tuples.time_place_scope: a British town in the shortage years of the 1940s
tuples.mechanism: imported fruit disappears and essences and acids stand in, so a wartime drink keeps the name while losing the ingredient
tuples.evidence_lens: food control orders and the labelling rules issued for substitute beverages

tuples.episode_object: a stoppered jug of effervescent spring water carried from a hillside seep
tuples.time_place_scope: a German spa valley in the visiting seasons of the 1700s
tuples.mechanism: naturally gassy springs are drunk as cures, and the wish to copy them is what starts the manufacture of an artificial water
tuples.evidence_lens: spa proprietors' price lists and the printed medical accounts of mineral springs

tuples.episode_object: a laboratory vessel of chalk and acid with a tube led down into water
tuples.time_place_scope: an English provincial laboratory in the experimental years of the 1760s
tuples.mechanism: gas released from chalk is dissolved into water under pressure, and a chemical demonstration becomes a manufacturing method
tuples.evidence_lens: scientific society papers and the laboratory notebooks kept by experimenters

tuples.episode_object: a glass domestic apparatus of stacked globes for charging water at home
tuples.time_place_scope: an English drawing room on a winter evening in the 1780s
tuples.mechanism: an instrument maker sells the process as furniture, and the drink is first bought as an apparatus rather than as a bottle
tuples.evidence_lens: instrument makers' catalogues and the household inventories listing such apparatus

tuples.episode_object: a lead pressure vessel and a hand pump in a small manufacturing yard
tuples.time_place_scope: a British mineral water works in the 1800s
tuples.mechanism: making gassed water in quantity needs pressure plant, and the trade moves from the drawing room into a licensed factory
tuples.evidence_lens: works plant inventories and the trade journals describing mineral water machinery

tuples.episode_object: a pharmacy shelf of labelled waters sold against stomach complaints
tuples.time_place_scope: a British dispensing shop in the prescribing years of the 1820s
tuples.mechanism: artificial waters are sold as medicines with stated mineral contents, so the drink is first retailed across a pharmacy counter
tuples.evidence_lens: apothecary registers and the printed pharmacopoeia entries for artificial waters

tuples.episode_object: a sample of bottled water found carrying metal from its own apparatus
tuples.time_place_scope: a British inspecting laboratory in the 1850s
tuples.mechanism: acid water attacks lead and copper plant, and public analysis forces a change to glass and tinned fittings across the trade
tuples.evidence_lens: public analyst reports and the manufacturers' plant specifications filed thereafter

tuples.episode_object: a wire-bound glass siphon with a lever tap and an internal tube
tuples.time_place_scope: a French bottling works in the manufacturing years of the 1830s
tuples.mechanism: keeping the gas in while pouring a little at a time needs a valved vessel, and the siphon makes repeated household use possible
tuples.evidence_lens: glassworks catalogues and the illustrated trade descriptions of siphon fittings

tuples.episode_object: a marble-topped counter with taps, syrup jars, and a draught arm
tuples.time_place_scope: an American city drug store in the 1870s
tuples.mechanism: gassed water is sold by the glass with syrups added to order, and the counter creates an entire retail trade of its own
tuples.evidence_lens: shop fitting catalogues and the drug store day books recording counter sales

tuples.episode_object: a licence certificate for a mineral water maker hung in a works office
tuples.time_place_scope: a British manufacturing town in the regulating years of the 1870s
tuples.mechanism: manufacture is licensed and inspected because the water supply itself is suspect, so drink law follows public health law
tuples.evidence_lens: local authority licensing registers and the sanitary inspection reports of works

tuples.episode_object: an egg-shaped bottle that cannot stand upright upon a shelf
tuples.time_place_scope: an English bottling works in the manufacturing years of the 1820s
tuples.mechanism: a cork must stay wet to hold gas, so the bottle is shaped to force it to lie down and the vessel enforces its own storage
tuples.evidence_lens: glassworks catalogues and the excavated bottle assemblages from urban sites

tuples.episode_object: a sawdust-packed ice chest beside a bottling works loading door
tuples.time_place_scope: a north American city yard in the summer weeks of the 1880s
tuples.mechanism: cold makes gas stay in solution, so ice is bought both for the filling room and for delivery through the hot months
tuples.evidence_lens: ice company delivery books and the works purchase accounts for summer supply

tuples.episode_object: a bar shelf of small bottles kept beside the spirit measures
tuples.time_place_scope: a London hotel bar through the evening trade of the 1890s
tuples.mechanism: gassed water is bought chiefly to dilute spirits, and a medicinal product finds its lasting market as an accompaniment
tuples.evidence_lens: hotel bar stock books and the printed drink tariffs of licensed premises

tuples.episode_object: a steel cylinder of compressed gas wheeled into a filling room
tuples.time_place_scope: a European bottling works through the working summers of the 1900s
tuples.mechanism: buying gas as a compressed industrial product ends on-site generation, and a supply industry grows behind the drink trade
tuples.evidence_lens: industrial gas company sale records and the works purchase and plant registers

tuples.episode_object: a works water tank fitted with a filter and a sealed sampling tap
tuples.time_place_scope: a British mineral water factory in the 1900s
tuples.mechanism: the drink is mostly water, so the source and its filtration become the main regulated part of the whole manufacture
tuples.evidence_lens: sanitary inspection reports and the works water analysis certificates

tuples.episode_object: a steamship saloon crate of small bottles listed in the stores book
tuples.time_place_scope: an ocean liner passage from a European port in the 1900s
tuples.mechanism: long voyages need drinks that keep, and shipboard service makes a bottled water a standard item of passenger provisioning
tuples.evidence_lens: ship stores accounts and the printed saloon tariffs carried aboard passenger vessels

tuples.episode_object: a printed label naming a German spring on a locally made bottle
tuples.time_place_scope: a British bottling works through the summer trade of the 1850s
tuples.mechanism: a place name is used as the description of a type, and naming becomes a dispute between imitators and the springs themselves
tuples.evidence_lens: trade circulars and the legal proceedings brought over the use of place names

tuples.episode_object: a canteen crate of gassed water set out beside a hot furnace floor
tuples.time_place_scope: an English ironworks in the working summers of the 1890s
tuples.mechanism: heavy heat work needs a safe drinking supply, and employers buy bottled water for reasons of production as much as welfare
tuples.evidence_lens: factory welfare committee minutes and the works purchase accounts for canteens

tuples.episode_object: a returnable household siphon collected weekly by a delivery cart
tuples.time_place_scope: a central European city street in the 1900s
tuples.mechanism: a deposit on the vessel makes household delivery viable, and the round rather than the shop becomes the channel of sale
tuples.evidence_lens: delivery round books and the deposit and returns records kept by bottling works

tuples.episode_object: a wartime notice restricting glass and metal for drink containers
tuples.time_place_scope: a British works office in the controlled years of the 1940s
tuples.mechanism: materials rather than ingredients limit output, and a drink industry is shaped by the allocation of glass, steel, and gas
tuples.evidence_lens: government control orders and the works correspondence with materials boards

tuples.episode_object: a pressure gauge and a temperature chart pinned above a carbonating tank
tuples.time_place_scope: a bottling works control room in the 1930s
tuples.mechanism: the amount of gas held depends on pressure and cold together, and understanding that relation is what makes output consistent
tuples.evidence_lens: works process records and the technical handbooks written for the bottling trade

tuples.episode_object: a basket of dried rye crusts saved from a household baking week
tuples.time_place_scope: a village house in the Russian countryside through the 1700s
tuples.mechanism: stale bread holds usable starch, so the drink begins as a way of turning a household leftover into something worth drinking
tuples.evidence_lens: household inventories and the ethnographic surveys of village food practice

tuples.episode_object: a wooden tub of soaked bread left under cloth beside a warm stove
tuples.time_place_scope: a peasant cottage in the Russian north in the mild weeks of spring, 1800s
tuples.mechanism: wild yeast and lactic bacteria work together at low strength, so the drink is barely alcoholic and is remade every few days
tuples.evidence_lens: ethnographic field surveys and the later laboratory analyses of traditional samples

tuples.episode_object: a monastery cellar of large tubs kept for the house and for the poor
tuples.time_place_scope: a Russian monastery in the working seasons of the 1600s
tuples.mechanism: religious houses make it in bulk for guests and alms, so charity rather than sale carries the drink through whole cities
tuples.evidence_lens: monastic cellarer accounts and the almsgiving records of religious houses

tuples.episode_object: a barrel on a two-wheeled cart with a brass tap and a stack of glasses
tuples.time_place_scope: a Russian city street in the hot months of the 1800s
tuples.mechanism: sale from a wheeled barrel puts the maker in the street, and pitch, licence, and glass washing become the trade's regulation
tuples.evidence_lens: municipal licence registers and the police records of street trading pitches

tuples.episode_object: a bowl of cold soup made with the drink poured over chopped vegetables
tuples.time_place_scope: a Russian household kitchen in the summer weeks of the 1800s
tuples.mechanism: the drink is also an ingredient, so its making is tied to a summer dish and its sourness is judged for cooking as well
tuples.evidence_lens: printed cookery books and the household account books of provincial families

tuples.episode_object: a field flask carried out to the harvest with a linen stopper
tuples.time_place_scope: a Russian estate at the reaping of the 1800s
tuples.mechanism: a low-strength sour drink replaces water in the field, and provisioning the harvest is part of what an estate must supply
tuples.evidence_lens: estate provisioning accounts and the labour agreements setting food and drink

tuples.episode_object: an inspection notice fixed to a street barrel about the washing of glasses
tuples.time_place_scope: a Russian provincial city in the 1900s, where shared street-barrel glasses were inspected for hygiene
tuples.mechanism: shared glasses at a street barrel become a public health question, and regulation attaches to the service, not the recipe
tuples.evidence_lens: sanitary inspection reports and the municipal by-laws on street drink selling

tuples.episode_object: a crown-capped bottle of the drink made in a small city works
tuples.time_place_scope: a Russian bottling works in the trading summers of the 1900s
tuples.mechanism: an unstable living drink resists bottling, and pasteurising or filtering it changes the taste that made it worth selling
tuples.evidence_lens: works production records and the trade journals describing bottling difficulties

tuples.episode_object: a crock where dried pears and honey are added to a fermenting tub
tuples.time_place_scope: a Ukrainian farm kitchen in the fruit season of the 1800s
tuples.mechanism: fruit and honey give sweetness and a second fermentation, and regional recipes multiply around one basic household method
tuples.evidence_lens: regional recipe collections and the ethnographic surveys of household drink making

tuples.episode_object: a field kitchen barrel drawn behind a supply wagon on a march
tuples.time_place_scope: an eastern European campaign road in the 1800s
tuples.mechanism: an army must drink safely on the move, and a soured drink made from ration bread is issued for health as much as for morale
tuples.evidence_lens: quartermaster provisioning records and the military medical reports of the period

tuples.episode_object: a state factory tank room with pipes running through to a filling hall
tuples.time_place_scope: a Soviet city works in the production years of the 1930s
tuples.mechanism: a household drink is standardised into a planned product, and recipe, strength, and price are set by central specification
tuples.evidence_lens: state standards documents and the factory production plans and output reports

tuples.episode_object: a kiln of sprouted rye dried dark for the drink's colour and taste
tuples.time_place_scope: a malting works in the western Russian lands in the 1800s
tuples.mechanism: roasted malt replaces bread in commercial making, so an industrial input quietly displaces the household leftover
tuples.evidence_lens: malting works accounts and the technical manuals written for the drink trade

tuples.episode_object: a printed dinner menu in a city house omitting the drink entirely
tuples.time_place_scope: a Russian noble household in the fashionable decades of the 1800s
tuples.mechanism: the drink is dismissed as common by an elite copying foreign tables, so class rather than taste drives it out of certain houses
tuples.evidence_lens: household menu books and the memoirs and travellers' accounts describing tables

tuples.episode_object: a barrel wheeled out of a tenement yard toward a factory street
tuples.time_place_scope: an industrial quarter of a Russian city in the 1890s
tuples.mechanism: migrants from villages bring the drink into factory districts, and urban work rather than rural custom keeps the trade alive
tuples.evidence_lens: city trade registers and the factory district surveys of food and drink sellers

tuples.episode_object: an ice cellar of packed river ice beneath a cooper-built storage barrel
tuples.time_place_scope: a Russian town yard in the winters of the 1800s
tuples.mechanism: a live drink spoils fast in heat, so cut ice and sound cooperage decide how far and how long it can actually be sold
tuples.evidence_lens: town ice trade records and the cooperage accounts kept by drink sellers

tuples.episode_object: a shop shelf card separating the drink from sweetened fizzy waters
tuples.time_place_scope: a Russian city grocery in the 1900s, where shop cards distinguished kvass from fizzy waters
tuples.mechanism: a legal definition is written to protect a fermented drink from imitation, and naming rules follow the arrival of competitors
tuples.evidence_lens: state standards documents and the trade circulars issued to retail sellers

tuples.episode_object: a fast-day table set with bread, salted vegetables, and a jug of the drink
tuples.time_place_scope: a Russian household during a church fast in the 1800s
tuples.mechanism: a long fasting calendar shapes what may be drunk, and a low-strength grain drink is permitted where stronger ones are not
tuples.evidence_lens: church fasting rules and the household provisioning accounts kept for fast periods

tuples.episode_object: a complaint book entry about a barrel found watered at a street pitch
tuples.time_place_scope: a Russian provincial market in the 1900s
tuples.mechanism: sale by the glass from a barrel invites dilution, so inspection of the sellers rather than the makers becomes the usual remedy
tuples.evidence_lens: market inspection records and the municipal complaint and prosecution registers

tuples.episode_object: a yellow tanker trailer parked at a city corner with a queue beside it
tuples.time_place_scope: a Soviet city street in the summer months of the 1970s
tuples.mechanism: bulk distribution by road tanker revives street sale at scale, and the drink returns as an organised municipal service
tuples.evidence_lens: municipal trade organisation records and the distribution plans of the period

tuples.episode_object: a physician's note recommending the drink for a weak appetite
tuples.time_place_scope: a Russian provincial practice in the 1800s
tuples.mechanism: sourness and live culture give it a digestive reputation, and medical advice keeps it in households that had otherwise left it
tuples.evidence_lens: medical practice notes and the printed household health manuals of the period

tuples.episode_object: a hollowed gourd and a woven strainer of split cane at a forest camp
tuples.time_place_scope: a Guarani settlement in the upper Parana forests in the 1500s
tuples.mechanism: an evergreen forest tree is gathered from wild stands and drunk in company long before any colonial record describes it
tuples.evidence_lens: early missionary and travellers' accounts read beside the archaeology of settlements

tuples.episode_object: a mission plantation of shaded seedlings raised in a nursery bed
tuples.time_place_scope: a Jesuit mission in the Parana basin in the working years of the 1700s
tuples.mechanism: learning to germinate a difficult seed turns a wild harvest into a planted crop, and mission economies are built upon it
tuples.evidence_lens: mission account books and the administrative reports of religious establishments

tuples.episode_object: a silver straw with a flattened strainer set in a hide-bound gourd
tuples.time_place_scope: a Buenos Aires household in the fashionable decades of the 1800s
tuples.mechanism: the utensils are made in precious metal for display, and silversmithing turns a drinking method into an object of status
tuples.evidence_lens: probate inventories and the silversmiths' order books of the river cities

tuples.episode_object: a green branch passed quickly through a flame above an open pit
tuples.time_place_scope: a forest gathering camp in the Paraguayan highlands in the 1800s
tuples.mechanism: a brief scorching stops the leaf from turning black, and that first step in the forest decides the colour of the finished leaf
tuples.evidence_lens: agricultural treatises on the crop and the field reports of trade inspectors

tuples.episode_object: a raft of leaf sacks poled down a brown river toward a landing
tuples.time_place_scope: a river passage down the Parana in the shipping season of the 1700s
tuples.mechanism: rivers rather than roads carry a bulky light cargo, and the market is drawn by where boats can reach and still return
tuples.evidence_lens: river port registers and the merchant accounts of consignments carried downstream

tuples.episode_object: a labour contract and an advance store account in a forest camp office
tuples.time_place_scope: a Paraguayan gathering camp in the working years of the 1880s
tuples.mechanism: advances against future wages tie gatherers to camps by debt, and the ledger is where that coercion is set down in figures
tuples.evidence_lens: camp store accounts, labour contracts, and the government inspection reports

tuples.episode_object: a colonial customs certificate for leaf leaving a river province
tuples.time_place_scope: a Rio de la Plata customs post in the 1700s
tuples.mechanism: a colonial administration taxes and licenses the trade, and revenue from one leaf supports a whole provincial government
tuples.evidence_lens: customs registers and the colonial treasury accounts of provincial revenue

tuples.episode_object: a single gourd refilled and passed in turn around a seated circle
tuples.time_place_scope: a ranch kitchen on the Argentine plain in the mornings of the 1800s
tuples.mechanism: one vessel served by one person to a group makes drinking an act of inclusion, and the etiquette of the round is strictly kept
tuples.evidence_lens: travellers' accounts and the ethnographic surveys of rural household custom

tuples.episode_object: a merchant's ledger of unfilled orders during a closed river war
tuples.time_place_scope: a river port on the Parana in the disrupted years of the 1860s
tuples.mechanism: a war cuts a producing region off from its buyers, and neighbouring countries plant their own stands to replace the supply
tuples.evidence_lens: merchant ledgers and the wartime trade and customs records of river ports

tuples.episode_object: a nursery row of seedlings raised under lath shade on a red soil field
tuples.time_place_scope: a Misiones plantation in the 1900s, where shaded nursery seedlings moved yerba mate onto farms
tuples.mechanism: domestication moves the crop out of the forest onto cleared farms, so yields rise while the old gathering camps decline
tuples.evidence_lens: agricultural station reports and the plantation planting and yield registers

tuples.episode_object: a wooden bin where dried leaf is kept for months before milling
tuples.time_place_scope: a processing works in southern Brazil in the 1900s
tuples.mechanism: resting the dried leaf softens its harshness, and a period of controlled storage becomes part of the definition of quality
tuples.evidence_lens: works process records and the trade standards describing curing and ageing

tuples.episode_object: a printed paper packet stating a grade by the proportion of stem
tuples.time_place_scope: a river city packing house in the packing weeks of the 1900s
tuples.mechanism: grading by leaf and stem gives buyers a shared vocabulary, and packaging turns a bulk commodity into a retail product
tuples.evidence_lens: trade circulars and the published grade standards written for packed leaf

tuples.episode_object: a pharmacy jar of dried leaf sold against fatigue and headache
tuples.time_place_scope: a European dispensing shop in the working weeks of the 1800s
tuples.mechanism: an imported leaf is offered as a medicinal stimulant abroad, and pharmacy rather than grocery is its first foreign counter
tuples.evidence_lens: apothecary registers and the printed materia medica entries for the leaf

tuples.episode_object: a saddlebag kettle, a gourd, and a leather roll of leaf on a ranch horse
tuples.time_place_scope: the open plains of the Argentine interior in the 1800s
tuples.mechanism: a portable hot drink suits a mounted working life, and the kit is designed around a fire, a horse, and a long distance
tuples.evidence_lens: travellers' accounts and the estancia provisioning accounts of ranch supplies

tuples.episode_object: a shipping case of packed leaf addressed to an eastern Mediterranean port
tuples.time_place_scope: a river city export house in the shipping seasons of the 1900s
tuples.mechanism: returning migrants carry the habit home with them, and a diaspora creates a durable export market on a distant coast
tuples.evidence_lens: export shipping manifests and the emigration and return records of the period

tuples.episode_object: a belt-driven mill with sieves grading leaf, stem, and powder
tuples.time_place_scope: a processing works in northern Argentina in the 1920s
tuples.mechanism: machine milling and screening replace hand pounding, and consistency of grind becomes something a factory can guarantee
tuples.evidence_lens: works plant inventories and the machinery trade catalogues of the period

tuples.episode_object: a regulatory board notice setting a minimum price for green leaf
tuples.time_place_scope: an Argentine producing province in the regulating years of the 1930s
tuples.mechanism: overplanting collapses prices, and a state board fixes plantings and prices in order to hold small growers on their land
tuples.evidence_lens: regulatory board records and the published price and planting regulations

tuples.episode_object: a bulked sample found mixed with the leaves of unrelated shrubs
tuples.time_place_scope: a provincial inspection office in the 1900s
tuples.mechanism: a milled leaf hides its origins, so botanical inspection under a lens becomes the way substitution is detected and punished
tuples.evidence_lens: inspection laboratory reports and the prosecution records for adulterated leaf

tuples.episode_object: a paper filter bag of milled leaf brewed like tea in an ordinary cup
tuples.time_place_scope: a city kitchen in southern Brazil in the 1900s
tuples.mechanism: brewing without the gourd removes the sharing and the utensil, so the same leaf becomes an entirely different domestic drink
tuples.evidence_lens: trade catalogues and the household cookery books describing preparation methods

tuples.episode_object: a public health notice discouraging a shared straw during an epidemic
tuples.time_place_scope: a South American city in the epidemic years of the 1910s
tuples.mechanism: communal drinking meets public health advice, and custom is defended, adapted, and only partly changed by official warning
tuples.evidence_lens: public health circulars and the newspaper record of the advice and its reception

tuples.episode_object: a wide crock of sweetened black tea with a pale mat floating on top
tuples.time_place_scope: a household kitchen in north-east China in the 1800s
tuples.mechanism: yeasts and acid bacteria live together in a mat at the surface, and sugar and tea are simply what the culture is fed on
tuples.evidence_lens: later microbiological studies read beside ethnographic accounts of household use

tuples.episode_object: a saucer holding a cut piece of culture wrapped in a damp cloth
tuples.time_place_scope: a neighbourhood in a Russian provincial town in the 1900s
tuples.mechanism: the culture grows and is divided, so it spreads as a gift between households and never through a commercial channel
tuples.evidence_lens: household correspondence and the ethnographic surveys of domestic food practice

tuples.episode_object: a travelling case with a sealed jar carried west along a rail line
tuples.time_place_scope: a journey across the Russian empire in the 1900s
tuples.mechanism: a living culture travels with people rather than as cargo, and its diffusion follows railways, migrations, and family ties
tuples.evidence_lens: travel diaries and the early European reports describing the drink's arrival

tuples.episode_object: a household jar fed with saccharin and weak tea during a shortage
tuples.time_place_scope: a central European kitchen in the scarce years of the 1940s
tuples.mechanism: when sugar and tea are rationed the culture is fed on substitutes and weakens, so scarcity is legible in the drink itself
tuples.evidence_lens: rationing records and the household diaries describing wartime kitchen practice

tuples.episode_object: a printed pamphlet listing complaints the drink is said to relieve
tuples.time_place_scope: a central European town in the publishing years of the 1920s
tuples.mechanism: claims circulate faster than evidence, and printed advice rather than any trial establishes what the drink is believed to do
tuples.evidence_lens: popular health pamphlets read critically beside the medical journals of the period

tuples.episode_object: a laboratory plate streaked from a sample of the floating mat
tuples.time_place_scope: a European microbiology laboratory in the 1910s
tuples.mechanism: culturing the organisms separately shows a community rather than one agent, and the drink is at last described scientifically
tuples.evidence_lens: published microbiological papers and the culture collection records of laboratories

tuples.episode_object: an official notice advising caution about home-fermented drinks
tuples.time_place_scope: a European public health office in the 1990s
tuples.mechanism: a home process with no controls raises contamination concerns, and health authorities answer with advice rather than a ban
tuples.evidence_lens: public health circulars and the case reports published in medical journals

tuples.episode_object: a titration flask measuring the acidity of a finished batch
tuples.time_place_scope: a food laboratory in the testing years of the 1990s
tuples.mechanism: acids accumulate as sugar is consumed, so a simple acidity measure shows how far a batch has gone and when to stop it
tuples.evidence_lens: published food chemistry studies and the laboratory method handbooks of the period

tuples.episode_object: a glass jar covered with woven cloth and secured by a rubber band
tuples.time_place_scope: a domestic kitchen in western Europe in the 1980s
tuples.mechanism: the culture needs air but not insects, so the covering rather than the vessel is the critical piece of household equipment
tuples.evidence_lens: printed home fermentation manuals and the household equipment catalogues

tuples.episode_object: an institute report on the drink circulated to regional health offices
tuples.time_place_scope: a Soviet research institute in the studying years of the 1950s
tuples.mechanism: a folk preparation is examined by a state research body, and official study lends it a standing that private claims could not
tuples.evidence_lens: institute research reports and the health administration circulars of the period

tuples.episode_object: a household guide printed with a diagram of a cloth-covered crock
tuples.time_place_scope: a central European household in the interwar years of the 1920s
tuples.mechanism: printed household guides carry the method between countries, so a domestic practice spreads through publishing not trade
tuples.evidence_lens: printed household manuals and the publishers' records of their circulation

tuples.episode_object: a bottled batch tested for the alcohol produced by its own yeasts
tuples.time_place_scope: a north American beverage laboratory in the 2010s
tuples.mechanism: a live drink keeps fermenting in the bottle, and regulators must decide at what strength it becomes an alcoholic beverage
tuples.evidence_lens: regulatory guidance documents and the laboratory test reports filed by producers

tuples.episode_object: a printed label arguing over whether the drink may be called a tea
tuples.time_place_scope: a north American labelling office in the 2010s
tuples.mechanism: naming determines which rules apply, so a dispute about one word decides taxation, shelf placement, and permitted claims
tuples.evidence_lens: labelling regulations and the trade correspondence with regulatory authorities

tuples.episode_object: a chilled cabinet of bottles kept below a stated storage temperature
tuples.time_place_scope: a retail grocery in a north American city in the 2010s
tuples.mechanism: cold slows a living product, so the cold chain rather than pasteurisation is what allows a live drink to be sold in shops
tuples.evidence_lens: retail storage standards and the distribution records of chilled beverage suppliers

tuples.episode_object: a padded envelope holding a dried culture sent between households
tuples.time_place_scope: a postal route between European towns in the 1990s
tuples.mechanism: a dried culture survives the post, and an informal exchange network moves living material without any commercial market
tuples.evidence_lens: amateur society newsletters and the postal exchange records of hobby networks

tuples.episode_object: a sealed second bottle with fruit juice added after the first ferment
tuples.time_place_scope: a home kitchen in western Europe in the 2000s
tuples.mechanism: a second closed fermentation makes gas and flavour together, and household practice adopts a technique borrowed from brewing
tuples.evidence_lens: printed home fermentation manuals and the amateur society journals of the period

tuples.episode_object: an inspection sheet for a small producer selling at a weekly market
tuples.time_place_scope: a market town in western Europe in the 2010s
tuples.mechanism: cottage production meets food safety law, and record keeping and acidity limits become the price of selling beyond a kitchen
tuples.evidence_lens: food safety inspection records and the registration files of small food producers

tuples.episode_object: a stainless vessel of a thousand litres fitted with a sampling port
tuples.time_place_scope: a contract beverage plant in north America in the 2010s
tuples.mechanism: scaling a surface-growing culture needs new vessel design, so industrial production reshapes the organism's growing conditions
tuples.evidence_lens: plant process records and the technical papers on scaled fermentation practice

tuples.episode_object: a nutrition panel stating residual sugar per bottle on a shop shelf
tuples.time_place_scope: a retail chiller in a north American city in the 2010s
tuples.mechanism: sugar is the culture's food and also a labelled dietary figure, so fermentation time is set partly by a printed number
tuples.evidence_lens: nutrition labelling regulations and the producers' compositional test records

tuples.episode_object: a shelf of self-published guides in a health food shop
tuples.time_place_scope: a north American city shop in the reviving years of the 1990s
tuples.mechanism: printed enthusiasm rather than institutions carries the practice into a new country, and publishing precedes any industry
tuples.evidence_lens: booksellers' records and the amateur society newsletters that circulated the method

tuples.episode_object: a tall plunge churn of staved wood with a cross-headed dash
tuples.time_place_scope: a farm kitchen in the west of Ireland through the summers of the 1700s
tuples.mechanism: butter is beaten out of cream and the thin liquid left behind is the drink, so one product exists only as another's residue
tuples.evidence_lens: farm inventories and the agricultural surveys describing dairy equipment

tuples.episode_object: a covered crock where cream is left to ripen for a day before churning
tuples.time_place_scope: a dairy in the Netherlands in the mild weeks of the 1600s
tuples.mechanism: letting cream sour first makes churning quicker and the residue tart, so taste follows from a purely practical decision
tuples.evidence_lens: dairy manuals and the estate accounts recording churning days and yields

tuples.episode_object: a glazed earthenware jar kept on the north wall of a stone-floored dairy
tuples.time_place_scope: an English farm dairy in the warm months of the 1700s
tuples.mechanism: an unheated north-facing room is the only refrigeration available, so building design is the dairy's preservation technology
tuples.evidence_lens: farm building accounts and the printed treatises on dairy construction

tuples.episode_object: a milking pail carried up from a hill pasture at the summer grazing
tuples.time_place_scope: a Norwegian mountain summer farm in the grazing months of the 1800s
tuples.mechanism: milk arrives in a flood in summer and stops in winter, so dairy drinks are seasonal and tied to where a herd is moved
tuples.evidence_lens: farm registers of summer grazing and the ethnographic surveys of mountain dairying

tuples.episode_object: a dairywoman's tally slate of butter made and milk set aside
tuples.time_place_scope: an English farm dairy in the working year of the 1700s
tuples.mechanism: dairying is women's work reckoned apart from the farm's grain, and the household's ready cash often comes from that account
tuples.evidence_lens: farm account books kept separately for the dairy and the probate inventories of farms

tuples.episode_object: a lidded churn carried to a town market on the back of a donkey
tuples.time_place_scope: a market road in southern Ireland in the trading mornings of the 1800s
tuples.mechanism: a perishable residue can be sold only within a few hours' travel, so the drink defines a small ring of country around a town
tuples.evidence_lens: market toll records and the day books kept by town dairy sellers

tuples.episode_object: a mixing bowl where the sour liquid meets a spoon of white powder
tuples.time_place_scope: an Irish farm kitchen in the baking mornings of the 1800s
tuples.mechanism: acid and a new alkaline powder raise bread without yeast, so a change in baking keeps a dairy by-product in daily demand
tuples.evidence_lens: printed cookery books and the grocers' records of powder and flour sales

tuples.episode_object: a servants' table jug set beside the household's butter and cream
tuples.time_place_scope: an English farmhouse at the midday meal of the 1700s
tuples.mechanism: the household keeps the butter and the workers are given the residue, so a food hierarchy is visible at a single table
tuples.evidence_lens: household provisioning accounts and the labour agreements listing diet allowances

tuples.episode_object: a physician's diet sheet naming the drink for a weak stomach
tuples.time_place_scope: a north European medical practice in the 1800s
tuples.mechanism: sour dairy is prescribed as easily digested, and medical advice keeps the drink respectable when fashion moves away from it
tuples.evidence_lens: printed household health manuals and the hospital diet records of the period

tuples.episode_object: a relief committee list of foods issued at a village depot
tuples.time_place_scope: an Irish district in the famine years of the 1840s
tuples.mechanism: a cheap dairy residue features in relief diets, so the records of hunger are also a record of what people ordinarily drank
tuples.evidence_lens: relief committee minutes and the government inquiry reports on distress

tuples.episode_object: a tank of pasteurised skimmed milk inoculated with a measured culture
tuples.time_place_scope: a north American creamery through the working year of the 1900s
tuples.mechanism: an industrial version is made by souring skimmed milk deliberately, so a by-product becomes a manufactured product of its own
tuples.evidence_lens: creamery process records and the published dairy standards for cultured products

tuples.episode_object: a hand-cranked centrifugal separator bolted to a dairy bench
tuples.time_place_scope: a Danish farm dairy in the changing decades of the 1880s
tuples.mechanism: spinning cream out of milk ends the long settling and moves butter making to creameries, so farms stop making the drink
tuples.evidence_lens: machinery trade catalogues and the creamery establishment and output records

tuples.episode_object: a dairy inspector's swab and a printed hygiene notice on a wall
tuples.time_place_scope: a British dairy in the 1900s, where dairy inspectors tested hygiene before sale
tuples.mechanism: milk-borne illness brings inspection into the dairy, and cleanliness rules rather than recipes decide what may be sold
tuples.evidence_lens: sanitary inspection reports and the local authority dairy registration records

tuples.episode_object: a sealed steel churn loaded into a ventilated railway van at dawn
tuples.time_place_scope: an English country station in the working mornings of the 1890s
tuples.mechanism: rail lets liquid dairy reach cities each morning, so a local product becomes a metropolitan supply governed by timetables
tuples.evidence_lens: railway consignment records and the dairy company delivery and receipt books

tuples.episode_object: a trough of the drink poured over ground barley in a farm pig yard
tuples.time_place_scope: a Danish farm in the fattening season of the 1890s
tuples.mechanism: when creameries take the milk the residue returns to the farm as feed, so pigs rather than people consume the surplus
tuples.evidence_lens: farm feeding accounts and the agricultural society reports on pig fattening

tuples.episode_object: a shop label distinguishing a cultured product from a churning residue
tuples.time_place_scope: a north American grocery in the 1900s, where labels distinguished cultured buttermilk from churning residue
tuples.mechanism: two different things share one name, so a definition must be written before a buyer can know which is in the bottle
tuples.evidence_lens: dairy standards documents and the trade circulars issued to retail sellers

tuples.episode_object: a bowl of the drink served cold beside boiled potatoes and salt
tuples.time_place_scope: a farm kitchen in the Low Countries at the midday meal of the 1800s
tuples.mechanism: a regional dish keeps the drink in daily use, so cookery rather than dairying explains where the custom survives longest
tuples.evidence_lens: regional cookery collections and the household account books of farm families

tuples.episode_object: a cooperative creamery share certificate held by a small farmer
tuples.time_place_scope: a Danish parish in the organising years of the 1880s
tuples.mechanism: farmers jointly own the processing plant, and the cooperative decides what is returned to members and what is sold on
tuples.evidence_lens: cooperative society minute books and the annual accounts distributed to members

tuples.episode_object: a domestic refrigerator shelf holding sealed cartons of fresh milk
tuples.time_place_scope: a north European kitchen in the changing years of the 1950s
tuples.mechanism: cold storage removes the need for a soured drink, and the household reason for making it disappears within a generation
tuples.evidence_lens: household appliance sale records and the dairy consumption surveys of the period

tuples.episode_object: a fast-day jug of thin sour milk set beside bread on a plain table
tuples.time_place_scope: a household in the Orthodox Balkans during a church fast in the 1800s
tuples.mechanism: religious rules divide foods by season, and a light dairy drink holds a defined place within a repeating fasting calendar
tuples.evidence_lens: church fasting rules and the household provisioning accounts kept for fast periods

tuples.episode_object: a grafted bitter orange growing in a walled irrigation garden
tuples.time_place_scope: an Andalusian garden town in the growing seasons of the 1100s
tuples.mechanism: the first oranges to reach Europe are bitter, and irrigation gardens rather than orchards are where the tree is first kept
tuples.evidence_lens: agricultural treatises of the period and the garden and irrigation records of towns

tuples.episode_object: a sweet orange scion bound onto a bitter rootstock in a nursery row
tuples.time_place_scope: a Portuguese coastal nursery in the planting decades of the 1500s
tuples.mechanism: a sweeter variety arrives by sea and spreads by grafting, so one imported cutting changes what a whole continent grows
tuples.evidence_lens: nursery records and the botanical correspondence describing new introductions

tuples.episode_object: a survey map of drained land laid out in numbered grove blocks
tuples.time_place_scope: a central Florida district in the settling years of the 1880s
tuples.mechanism: land companies sell groves to settlers, so citrus planting is a property scheme as much as an agricultural decision
tuples.evidence_lens: land company prospectuses and the county deed and settlement registers

tuples.episode_object: an iced railway car packed with wrapped fruit and bunkered with ice
tuples.time_place_scope: a southern American railhead in the shipping seasons of the 1890s
tuples.mechanism: iced rail cars let fresh fruit reach far markets, so the fruit trade precedes the juice trade by many decades
tuples.evidence_lens: railway consignment records and the fruit shippers' packing and shipping books

tuples.episode_object: a laboratory bench of measured animal diets and weighed citrus rations
tuples.time_place_scope: a European nutrition laboratory in the researching years of the 1920s
tuples.mechanism: an anti-scurvy factor is isolated and measured, and a fruit becomes valued for a named chemical rather than for its taste
tuples.evidence_lens: published nutrition studies and the laboratory records of feeding experiments

tuples.episode_object: a soldered can of juice processed for long storage
tuples.time_place_scope: an American cannery in the working years of the 1920s
tuples.mechanism: heat sterilising makes juice keep but changes its flavour, and preservation and taste are set against one another for decades
tuples.evidence_lens: cannery production records and the food technology journals reporting on trials

tuples.episode_object: a plate heat exchanger running juice through a brief high temperature
tuples.time_place_scope: a citrus processing plant in Florida in the 1940s
tuples.mechanism: a very short heating kills spoilage organisms with less flavour loss, so process engineering rescues the taste of stored juice
tuples.evidence_lens: plant process records and the published food engineering papers of the period

tuples.episode_object: a vacuum evaporator and a chilled store of concentrated juice blocks
tuples.time_place_scope: a Florida processing plant in the developing years of the 1940s
tuples.mechanism: removing water and adding a little fresh juice back gives a storable product, and concentrate creates a national market
tuples.evidence_lens: research station technical reports and the plant production and storage records

tuples.episode_object: a marketing order sheet setting how much fruit may be shipped fresh
tuples.time_place_scope: an American citrus growing district in the regulating years of the 1930s
tuples.mechanism: surplus is diverted into processing by rule, and juice grows as the planned outlet for fruit the fresh market cannot absorb
tuples.evidence_lens: marketing order records and the published grower committee decisions

tuples.episode_object: a printed breakfast menu listing a small glass before the cooked dish
tuples.time_place_scope: an American hotel dining room in the 1920s
tuples.mechanism: a meal custom is built by advertising and hotel service together, and juice becomes the accepted opening of a morning meal
tuples.evidence_lens: hotel menus and the trade press describing promotional campaigns of the period

tuples.episode_object: a refractometer and an acid titration set on a packing house bench
tuples.time_place_scope: a Florida packing house in the grading years of the 1930s
tuples.mechanism: sugar measured against acid gives a number for ripeness, so harvest dates and legal maturity are settled by an instrument
tuples.evidence_lens: state maturity standards and the packing house laboratory testing records

tuples.episode_object: a grove of blackened trees photographed after a hard frost
tuples.time_place_scope: a central Florida grove in the freezing winter of the 1890s
tuples.mechanism: a single freeze can destroy decades of planting, and the industry moves further south and insures itself against a repeat
tuples.evidence_lens: agricultural station damage reports and the insurance and county loss records

tuples.episode_object: a layered barrel of split herring packed with coarse crystals

tuples.episode_object: a camel load of cut salt slabs bound with cord for a desert crossing

tuples.episode_object: a cleared hillside of stumps standing behind a brine boiling house

tuples.episode_object: a small dish of salt set beside bread at a threshold greeting

tuples.episode_object: a pepper vine trained up a living support tree in a garden plot

tuples.episode_object: an apothecary jar of powdered bark kept for warming preparations

tuples.episode_object: a village register listing households owing peeling service by descent
