tuples.episode_object: a warehouse fire lit deliberately to reduce an oversupplied stock
tuples.time_place_scope: a company warehouse yard in a north European port in the 1600s
tuples.mechanism: burning surplus keeps a price high, and destruction of goods is used openly as an instrument of commercial policy
tuples.evidence_lens: company minute books and the warehouse stock and destruction records

tuples.episode_object: an apothecary drawer of buds weighed for a preparation against toothache
tuples.time_place_scope: a dispensing shop in a north European town in the 1500s
tuples.mechanism: the bud is classed as hot and drying and prescribed for pain and digestion, so medicine sustains demand between fashions
tuples.evidence_lens: apothecary registers and the printed herbals describing the bud's qualities

tuples.episode_object: an orange studded with buds and hung inside a linen press
tuples.time_place_scope: a household in northern Europe in the 1600s
tuples.mechanism: aromatics are used against moths and against bad air, so a spice is bought for the cupboard as much as for the pot
tuples.evidence_lens: household inventories and the domestic manuals recommending aromatic preparations

tuples.episode_object: a customs weighing beam and a duty schedule at a spice quay
tuples.time_place_scope: a European port in the collecting years of the 1600s
tuples.mechanism: a valuable light cargo is taxed by weight at landing, and the customs house becomes the trade's principal point of record
tuples.evidence_lens: port customs registers and the duty schedules published for imported spices

tuples.episode_object: a plantation register recording workers after emancipation was declared
tuples.time_place_scope: a Zanzibar estate in the changing years of the 1890s
tuples.mechanism: abolition forces estates to pay for picking, and the cost of a labour-heavy harvest changes a whole island economy
tuples.evidence_lens: colonial administration reports and the estate labour and wage registers

tuples.episode_object: a stoneware jar of pickled vegetables spiced with whole buds
tuples.time_place_scope: a north European household kitchen in the preserving weeks of the 1700s
tuples.mechanism: aromatic oils help preserve as well as flavour, so household preserving quietly consumes a steady share of the spice
tuples.evidence_lens: household receipt manuscripts and the printed preserving manuals of the period

tuples.episode_object: a printed paper packet holding a weighed ounce of whole buds
tuples.time_place_scope: a British grocery in the 1900s, where weighed clove packets replaced the grocer’s scoop
tuples.mechanism: small pre-weighed packets replace the shop scoop, and packaging turns an exotic import into an ordinary shelf item
tuples.evidence_lens: grocers' trade catalogues and the packaging records of spice merchant houses

tuples.episode_object: a cooperative buying record of buds delivered by smallholding families
tuples.time_place_scope: an Indonesian island district in the growing years of the 1980s
tuples.mechanism: a tree that yields heavily only in some years makes prices swing, so cooperatives try to steady a naturally uneven income
tuples.evidence_lens: cooperative buying records and the agricultural census returns of smallholdings

tuples.episode_object: a nutmeg tree grown beneath tall shade in a volcanic island grove
tuples.time_place_scope: a Banda island grove in the growing seasons of the 1500s
tuples.mechanism: the tree fruits only in a narrow island climate, so the entire early world supply comes from a handful of small islands
tuples.evidence_lens: early travellers' accounts and the trading company reports on island groves

tuples.episode_object: a split fruit showing a red lacy web wrapped around a brown seed
tuples.time_place_scope: a Banda island drying yard at the harvest of the 1600s
tuples.mechanism: one fruit yields two separately traded spices, and the first task after picking is to part them and dry them differently
tuples.evidence_lens: agricultural treatises and the company instructions issued on preparing the crop

tuples.episode_object: a tub of lime wash in which sound seeds are rolled before packing
tuples.time_place_scope: a company warehouse on a Maluku island in the 1600s
tuples.mechanism: coating the seed prevents it sprouting elsewhere, so a monopoly is enforced through a treatment applied before shipment
tuples.evidence_lens: company administrative orders and the warehouse preparation and packing records

tuples.episode_object: a resettlement register of islanders and incoming planters after a conquest
tuples.time_place_scope: a Banda island district in the violent years of the 1620s
tuples.mechanism: a population is destroyed and replaced by licensed planters, and a trade monopoly is built upon a deliberate depopulation
tuples.evidence_lens: company administrative records and the later historical inquiries into the events

tuples.episode_object: a licensed estate holding with a fixed delivery obligation to a warehouse
tuples.time_place_scope: a Banda island estate in the working years of the 1600s
tuples.mechanism: planters hold land only on condition of selling all produce at a set price, so property and monopoly are written together
tuples.evidence_lens: estate grant records and the company purchase and delivery account books

tuples.episode_object: a pierced silver ball holding a grated seed worn upon a chain
tuples.time_place_scope: a European city household in the plague years of the 1600s
tuples.mechanism: aromatics are believed to guard against bad air, so an epidemic raises the price of a spice far more than any recipe could
tuples.evidence_lens: household inventories and the printed plague advice literature of the period

tuples.episode_object: a company auction catalogue listing lots released for a season's sale
tuples.time_place_scope: a north European auction room in the trading years of the 1700s
tuples.mechanism: releasing stock slowly at auction keeps the price steady, so a monopoly is managed as a calendar as much as a cargo
tuples.evidence_lens: auction catalogues and the company minute books recording release decisions

tuples.episode_object: a case of young plants landed at a colonial island garden
tuples.time_place_scope: a Caribbean island colony in the planting years of the 1800s
tuples.mechanism: seedlings taken during a war are established in a new colony, and one island's monopoly becomes another island's staple
tuples.evidence_lens: botanical garden accession registers and the colonial agricultural reports

tuples.episode_object: a cloth-wrapped grater with a compartment for a single seed
tuples.time_place_scope: an English gentleman's coat pocket in the 1700s
tuples.mechanism: a spice grated at the moment of use suits a portable tool, and the utensil shows how much a small quantity is valued
tuples.evidence_lens: silversmiths' order books and the probate inventories listing pocket graters

tuples.episode_object: a turned wooden imitation seed found among a parcel of the real ones
tuples.time_place_scope: a European market inspection in the 1700s
tuples.mechanism: a high price invites crude counterfeits, and the story of wooden seeds outlives whatever its actual frequency may have been
tuples.evidence_lens: market inspection records and the merchant correspondence complaining of fraud

tuples.episode_object: a medical note warning against taking more than a small quantity
tuples.time_place_scope: a European medical practice in the 1500s
tuples.mechanism: the seed is known to be harmful in quantity, so dosage warnings accompany it in the medical literature from very early on
tuples.evidence_lens: printed medical works and the apothecary registers recording prescribed amounts

tuples.episode_object: a sealed packet of seeds carried away against an express prohibition
tuples.time_place_scope: an eastern Indonesian anchorage in the 1770s
tuples.mechanism: an enforced monopoly can be undone by a single successful theft, so plant transfer is pursued as a matter of state policy
tuples.evidence_lens: colonial correspondence and the botanical collecting reports of the expeditions

tuples.episode_object: a rack of split arils drying flat beneath a woven shade screen
tuples.time_place_scope: an island drying yard in the working seasons of the 1700s
tuples.mechanism: the lacy covering must be flattened and dried slowly to hold its colour, and appearance decides most of its selling price
tuples.evidence_lens: trade descriptions of preparation and the packing store inspection records

tuples.episode_object: a counting frame sorting seeds by how many fill a standard weight
tuples.time_place_scope: an island packing store in the sorting weeks of the 1800s
tuples.mechanism: size is graded by count per unit weight, so a simple counting rule gives distant buyers a shared and checkable standard
tuples.evidence_lens: published grade standards and the packing house sorting and weighing records

tuples.episode_object: a dairy bench where grated seed is stirred through a pot of warm milk
tuples.time_place_scope: a north European kitchen in the working evenings of the 1700s
tuples.mechanism: the spice suits dairy and sweet dishes, and household cookery rather than grand feasting keeps a steady demand alive
tuples.evidence_lens: printed cookery books and the household account books listing spice purchases

tuples.episode_object: a plantation report on trees blown down across a hillside estate
tuples.time_place_scope: a Caribbean island in the storm season of the 1950s
tuples.mechanism: a slow-growing tree destroyed by one storm takes years to replace, so a national export can be halted for a whole decade
tuples.evidence_lens: colonial agricultural reports and the storm damage and rehabilitation records

tuples.episode_object: a press extracting a solid fat from broken and unsound seeds
tuples.time_place_scope: an island processing shed in the working months of the 1900s
tuples.mechanism: damaged seed too poor for the spice trade yields a fat and an oil, and by-products decide what a low grade is worth
tuples.evidence_lens: works production records and the trade journals describing oil and fat extraction

tuples.episode_object: a customs schedule listing the two spices at different rates of duty
tuples.time_place_scope: a European customs house in the collecting seasons of the 1700s
tuples.mechanism: the covering and the seed are taxed separately, so a single fruit is split into two fiscal categories at the quayside
tuples.evidence_lens: customs registers and the duty schedules published for the two named spices

tuples.episode_object: a cooperative weighing station receiving sacks from hillside smallholders
tuples.time_place_scope: an Indonesian island district in the growing years of the 1980s
tuples.mechanism: production returns to smallholders after estates decline, and cooperative buying decides what a family's trees are worth
tuples.evidence_lens: cooperative buying records and the agricultural census returns of smallholdings

tuples.episode_object: a grocer's drawer of whole seeds sold singly across a counter
tuples.time_place_scope: a British grocery in the retail years of the 1800s
tuples.mechanism: sale by the single seed keeps a costly spice within reach, so retail practice adapts to what a household can afford at once
tuples.evidence_lens: grocers' day books and the printed price lists of retail spice merchants

tuples.episode_object: a basket of lifted corms sorted for replanting in a fresh field
tuples.time_place_scope: a La Mancha village field in the planting weeks of the 1700s
tuples.mechanism: the plant sets no useful seed, so it is multiplied by dividing corms and a field must be lifted and moved every few years
tuples.evidence_lens: agricultural treatises and the village land and planting records of the district

tuples.episode_object: a shallow basket of purple flowers picked before the sun is high
tuples.time_place_scope: a Persian upland field at the autumn flowering of the 1500s
tuples.mechanism: the flowers open for a few days only and must be picked at dawn, so harvest is a brief and total village mobilisation
tuples.evidence_lens: agricultural treatises and the travellers' accounts describing the flowering weeks

tuples.episode_object: a table of women pulling three red threads from each opened flower
tuples.time_place_scope: a village room in central Spain on autumn evenings in the 1800s
tuples.mechanism: separating the stigmas is done indoors on the same day, and the labour rather than the land is the crop's real cost
tuples.evidence_lens: village labour records and the ethnographic surveys of the harvest season

tuples.episode_object: a fine sieve of threads drying above a low charcoal heat
tuples.time_place_scope: a village drying room in central Spain in the 1800s
tuples.mechanism: drying fixes the colour and the aroma, and how it is done decides whether a crop meets the highest grade or the lowest
tuples.evidence_lens: published grade standards and the cooperative processing and drying records

tuples.episode_object: a market ledger recording a weight of threads against a weight of silver
tuples.time_place_scope: a north European trading town in the 1400s
tuples.mechanism: a great many flowers make a very little spice, so the yield ratio rather than scarcity of land explains the price
tuples.evidence_lens: market price currents and the merchant house accounts of purchase and sale

tuples.episode_object: a field of flowering corms grown on chalk beside a market town
tuples.time_place_scope: an English east midland district in the growing years of the 1500s
tuples.mechanism: a warm-climate crop is grown in the north while labour is cheap, and a town takes its name from a crop it will later lose
tuples.evidence_lens: borough records and the manorial and parish accounts of local cultivation

tuples.episode_object: a pile of adulterated threads burned publicly in a market square
tuples.time_place_scope: a south German trading city in the inspecting years of the 1400s
tuples.mechanism: a specialised inspection office tests and destroys fraudulent lots, and public burning is used to deter a profitable fraud
tuples.evidence_lens: city inspection ordinances and the court records of prosecutions for adulteration

tuples.episode_object: a sample found mixed with dyed safflower and shredded marigold petals
tuples.time_place_scope: a European inspection office in the 1900s
tuples.mechanism: cheap yellow flowers imitate the colour without the aroma, so microscopy and colour measurement become the standard test
tuples.evidence_lens: inspection laboratory reports and the published methods for detecting substitution

tuples.episode_object: a dyer's vat of yellow liquor with cloth lifted upon a wooden pole
tuples.time_place_scope: a north European dye house in the working weeks of the 1400s
tuples.mechanism: the same threads colour cloth and food, so the dyeing trade competes with the kitchen for one limited annual harvest
tuples.evidence_lens: dyers' guild records and the workshop accounts of dyestuffs purchased

tuples.episode_object: a scribe's shell of yellow pigment beside a half-finished initial
tuples.time_place_scope: a monastic writing room in northern Europe in the 1200s
tuples.mechanism: the threads yield a transparent yellow for manuscript work, so a costly food is bought by libraries as an artist's material
tuples.evidence_lens: monastic library accounts and the technical analyses made of manuscript pigments

tuples.episode_object: an apothecary jar of threads weighed for a preparation against melancholy
tuples.time_place_scope: a dispensing shop in a north Italian city in the 1500s
tuples.mechanism: the spice is prescribed for the spirits and for the eyes, and medical reputation supports a price cookery alone could not
tuples.evidence_lens: apothecary registers and the printed pharmacopoeia entries for the preparation

tuples.episode_object: a bowl of threads steeped in warm milk for a temple offering
tuples.time_place_scope: a south Indian temple in the festival seasons of the 1600s
tuples.mechanism: colour is used to mark sanctity, so religious use holds a steady demand quite separate from cookery or from medicine
tuples.evidence_lens: temple endowment records and the ritual manuals describing offerings and supplies

tuples.episode_object: a sealed customs bale weighed against a schedule of very high rates
tuples.time_place_scope: a Mediterranean port in the collecting years of the 1400s
tuples.mechanism: the highest value by weight of any spice makes it the most attractive to tax, and it is watched more closely than any other
tuples.evidence_lens: port customs registers and the toll schedules published for imported spices

tuples.episode_object: a caravan chest of packed threads carried overland toward a Black Sea port
tuples.time_place_scope: a route from the Iranian plateau westward in the 1300s
tuples.mechanism: a light and enormously valuable good justifies overland carriage, and inland routes stay viable where bulky goods cannot pay
tuples.evidence_lens: caravan merchant letters and the port registers of goods landed from the interior

tuples.episode_object: a village council roll assigning picking turns among neighbouring households
tuples.time_place_scope: a La Mancha village in the harvest days of the 1800s
tuples.mechanism: a harvest that must be finished in a week is organised as reciprocal labour, so custom rather than wages fills the fields
tuples.evidence_lens: village council records and the ethnographic surveys of harvest labour exchange

tuples.episode_object: a bundle of unsold English threads beside a bill for imported ones
tuples.time_place_scope: an English market town in the declining years of the 1700s
tuples.mechanism: rising wages make a labour-heavy crop unprofitable in the north, and cultivation retreats to where labour is cheapest
tuples.evidence_lens: market price records and the agricultural surveys reporting on abandoned crops

tuples.episode_object: a laboratory cell measuring colour strength in a dissolved sample
tuples.time_place_scope: a European testing laboratory in the 1980s
tuples.mechanism: colour, aroma, and bitterness are measured as numbers, and an international grading standard replaces the buyer's own nose
tuples.evidence_lens: published international grading standards and the laboratory test certificates

tuples.episode_object: a wide pan of rice coloured through with a spoonful of steeped threads
tuples.time_place_scope: a Valencian kitchen at a Sunday meal in the 1800s
tuples.mechanism: a regional dish anchors demand inside a producing country, so local cookery protects a crop when export markets weaken
tuples.evidence_lens: printed regional cookery books and the household accounts of provincial families

tuples.episode_object: a lifted corm showing rot in a field left too long unmoved
tuples.time_place_scope: a Mediterranean growing district in the 1900s
tuples.mechanism: disease builds in soil that carries the crop too long, so rotation and clean planting stock are the growers' main defence
tuples.evidence_lens: agricultural station reports and the plant health inspection records of districts

tuples.episode_object: a protected name certificate issued for threads grown in one district
tuples.time_place_scope: a European producing district in the registering years of the 1990s
tuples.mechanism: a district registers its name in law to hold off cheaper imports, so geography becomes the growers' last commercial defence
tuples.evidence_lens: protected designation registers and the cooperative inspection and audit records

tuples.episode_object: a climbing vine trained through the branches of a shade tree
tuples.time_place_scope: a lowland forest garden on the Mexican gulf coast in the 1500s
tuples.mechanism: an orchid grown as a climber needs a living support and partial shade, so cultivation copies the forest rather than a field
tuples.evidence_lens: early colonial accounts and the later botanical descriptions of the growing regions

tuples.episode_object: a flower opening for a single morning above a leaf axil
tuples.time_place_scope: a coastal Mexican plantation at the flowering season of the 1700s
tuples.mechanism: the flower is open for hours only and set by particular local insects, so transplanted vines abroad flower without fruiting
tuples.evidence_lens: botanical papers and the plantation flowering and fruiting observation records

tuples.episode_object: a slender bamboo splinter used to lift a flap and press two parts together
tuples.time_place_scope: an island plantation in the western Indian ocean in the 1840s
tuples.mechanism: a simple hand method for setting the flower makes cultivation possible abroad, so one technique opens up a world crop
tuples.evidence_lens: botanical garden reports and the plantation records describing pollination practice

tuples.episode_object: a crate of green pods scalded in hot water and wrapped in blankets
tuples.time_place_scope: a curing yard on an Indian ocean island in the 1900s
tuples.mechanism: killing, sweating, drying, and conditioning over months develop the aroma, so most of the value is made after picking
tuples.evidence_lens: curing station process records and the agricultural station technical bulletins

tuples.episode_object: a planting register of cuttings distributed to island smallholders
tuples.time_place_scope: a Madagascar coastal district in the 1900s, where planting cuttings were distributed to island smallholders
tuples.mechanism: cultivation is spread among small farms rather than estates, so a world crop rests upon many thousands of small holdings
tuples.evidence_lens: colonial agricultural reports and the district planting and distribution registers

tuples.episode_object: a night watchman's lamp and a numbered mark pricked into each pod
tuples.time_place_scope: a Madagascar smallholding in the ripening weeks of the 1900s
tuples.mechanism: a small high-value crop invites theft, and marking and guarding become a normal part of the cost of growing it
tuples.evidence_lens: police and district administration records and the growers' association reports

tuples.episode_object: a chemical works vessel producing a flavour compound from wood liquor
tuples.time_place_scope: a European chemical works in the manufacturing years of the 1870s
tuples.mechanism: a single compound responsible for much of the aroma can be made industrially, and a farm crop meets a factory substitute
tuples.evidence_lens: chemical trade journals and the works production records of the period

tuples.episode_object: a printed label distinguishing an extract from an imitation flavouring
tuples.time_place_scope: a north American labelling office in the 1900s, where labels distinguished vanilla extract from imitation flavouring
tuples.mechanism: law is written to separate the pod's extract from the made compound, so one word on a label divides two whole industries
tuples.evidence_lens: labelling regulations and the standards of identity published for flavourings

tuples.episode_object: a market report of prices multiplying after a season of storms
tuples.time_place_scope: an Indian ocean island market in the cyclone years of the 2000s
tuples.mechanism: a concentrated growing region and a long lag between planting and harvest make the price swing extremely violently
tuples.evidence_lens: market price reports and the meteorological and crop damage assessments

tuples.episode_object: a jug of ground cacao paste scented with a single split pod
tuples.time_place_scope: a household in the Valley of Mexico in the years around the 1500s
tuples.mechanism: the pod is first used to scent a chocolate drink, so its earliest recorded purpose is as a flavouring inside another drink
tuples.evidence_lens: early colonial accounts and the illustrated manuscripts describing preparation

tuples.episode_object: a hand-cranked ice cream freezer with a paper of split pods beside it
tuples.time_place_scope: an American household kitchen in the 1800s
tuples.mechanism: frozen sweets need a flavour that survives cold, and confectionery becomes by far the largest single use of the pod
tuples.evidence_lens: printed cookery books and the confectioners' purchase and production records

tuples.episode_object: a grading bench where pods are laid against a marked measuring board
tuples.time_place_scope: an island packing store in the grading weeks of the 1900s
tuples.mechanism: length, moisture, and appearance set the grade, so measurement after curing decides what an entire crop is worth
tuples.evidence_lens: published grade standards and the packing store measurement and sorting records

tuples.episode_object: a curing station's receipt book for green pods brought in by growers
tuples.time_place_scope: a Madagascar district curing station in the 1950s
tuples.mechanism: growers sell green and processors capture the curing value, so where the pods are cured decides where the profit stays
tuples.evidence_lens: curing station receipt books and the district trade and buying records

tuples.episode_object: a colonial tribute list naming cured pods among goods owed by a district
tuples.time_place_scope: a gulf coast province of colonial Mexico in the 1600s
tuples.mechanism: a wild-gathered crop is demanded as tribute, so colonial extraction rather than trade first moves it in any quantity
tuples.evidence_lens: tribute rolls and the colonial provincial administration and revenue records

tuples.episode_object: a perfumer's flask of alcoholic extract on a blending bench
tuples.time_place_scope: a French perfume workshop in the 1900s, where vanilla extract was blended for perfume as well as food
tuples.mechanism: the pod's soft base note is used in scent as well as in food, so perfumery competes with confectionery for one crop
tuples.evidence_lens: perfumery house formula books and the purchase records for raw materials

tuples.episode_object: a lot of pods found soaked and weighted before a sale made by weight
tuples.time_place_scope: an importing port inspection office in the 1900s
tuples.mechanism: sale by weight invites added moisture, so moisture testing on arrival becomes the buyer's principal protection
tuples.evidence_lens: port inspection laboratory reports and the trade contract standards for moisture

tuples.episode_object: an export licence stamped for a consignment leaving an island port
tuples.time_place_scope: an Indian ocean island customs office in the 1960s
tuples.mechanism: a state marketing board licenses exports and sets a floor price, so a small country's whole trade is managed by decree
tuples.evidence_lens: marketing board records and the export licensing files of the customs service

tuples.episode_object: a laboratory rack of vine cuttings raised in sterile glass jars
tuples.time_place_scope: a tropical agricultural research station in the 1980s
tuples.mechanism: raising planting material free of virus protects a crop that has been propagated only by cuttings for generations
tuples.evidence_lens: research station technical reports and the plant health certification records

tuples.episode_object: a day list of vines to be pollinated before the morning heat
tuples.time_place_scope: a smallholding in an Indian ocean island district in the 1900s
tuples.mechanism: every flower must be set by hand within hours, so harvest is limited by how many vines one person can reach in a morning
tuples.evidence_lens: growers' association records and the agricultural extension reports on labour needs

tuples.episode_object: a customs entry classing cured pods separately from flavour extracts
tuples.time_place_scope: a European customs house on a routine clearing day in the 1900s
tuples.mechanism: pods, extracts, and made compounds carry different duties, so classification at the border shapes where processing is done
tuples.evidence_lens: customs classification records and the tariff rulings published on flavour goods

tuples.episode_object: a seed store of small wild fruits kept beside larger cultivated pods
tuples.time_place_scope: a highland Mexican settlement in the centuries before the 1400s
tuples.mechanism: several species are domesticated separately from wild ancestors, and selection for size and heat is thousands of years old
tuples.evidence_lens: archaeobotanical remains from cave and settlement sites and later botanical studies

tuples.episode_object: a bundle of dried pods carried aboard a returning Atlantic ship
tuples.time_place_scope: an Iberian port at the landing of a voyage in the 1490s
tuples.mechanism: a plant that grows from seed anywhere warm spreads faster than a monopoly can be built, so no trade control ever forms
tuples.evidence_lens: early voyage accounts and the botanical and herbal descriptions written soon after

tuples.episode_object: a market stall of red pods sold beside older and dearer black corns
tuples.time_place_scope: a west Indian coastal market in the trading years of the 1500s
tuples.mechanism: a cheap local heat replaces an expensive import, and adoption is fastest where the older spice was hardest to afford
tuples.evidence_lens: travellers' accounts and the market and revenue records of coastal districts

tuples.episode_object: a slatted rack of pods hung above a slow smouldering wood fire
tuples.time_place_scope: a highland Mexican farm in the drying weeks of the 1600s
tuples.mechanism: smoke dries and preserves the fruit and adds its own flavour, so a preservation method becomes a distinct regional ingredient
tuples.evidence_lens: agricultural and cookery manuals and the ethnographic surveys of farm practice

tuples.episode_object: a stone mill grinding dried pods with cumin and garlic into a paste
tuples.time_place_scope: a north Indian kitchen in the working mornings of the 1700s
tuples.mechanism: the fruit is absorbed into existing spice mixtures rather than used alone, so a new import is naturalised through blending
tuples.evidence_lens: recipe manuscripts and the printed regional cookery collections of the period

tuples.episode_object: a crock of salted mashed pods left to sour beneath a wooden lid
tuples.time_place_scope: a southern Chinese farm kitchen in the preserving weeks of the 1700s
tuples.mechanism: salting and souring makes a keeping condiment, so a seasonal fruit becomes a year-round staple in a single household step
tuples.evidence_lens: regional cookery collections and the ethnographic surveys of preserving practice

tuples.episode_object: a smallholder's field of staked plants set between rows of maize
tuples.time_place_scope: a Mexican highland farm in the growing season of the 1800s
tuples.mechanism: the crop is grown in small mixed plots for household use and local sale, and it never becomes a plantation commodity at home
tuples.evidence_lens: agricultural census returns and the district market and land use records

tuples.episode_object: a tasting panel of diluted samples scored by a row of assessors
tuples.time_place_scope: an American laboratory in the measuring years of the 1910s
tuples.mechanism: heat is first measured by how far a sample must be diluted before it is no longer felt, and sensation becomes a number
tuples.evidence_lens: published laboratory methods and the assessment records of testing panels

tuples.episode_object: a jar of oil and vinegar packed with whole pods on a pantry shelf
tuples.time_place_scope: a southern European kitchen in the preserving weeks of the 1800s
tuples.mechanism: acid and oil keep the fruit through winter, so preserving rather than fresh use is how most households actually eat it
tuples.evidence_lens: printed preserving manuals and the household account books of provincial families

tuples.episode_object: a plaster of ground pods spread on cloth for aching joints
tuples.time_place_scope: a European dispensing shop in the working weeks of the 1800s
tuples.mechanism: the fruit is used to draw blood to the skin as a counter-irritant, so pharmacy keeps it in stock quite apart from cookery
tuples.evidence_lens: apothecary registers and the printed pharmacopoeia entries for the preparation

tuples.episode_object: a tribute list naming dried pods among the goods owed by a district
tuples.time_place_scope: a tributary province of central Mexico in the 1400s
tuples.mechanism: a staple crop is demanded as tribute beside maize and cloth, and its importance is measured by the state's own accounting
tuples.evidence_lens: tribute rolls and the pictorial registers listing goods owed by each district

tuples.episode_object: a herbal page giving the new fruit the name of an older spice
tuples.time_place_scope: a European printing town in the describing years of the 1500s
tuples.mechanism: a new plant is named after the trade it displaces, and a confusion of names outlives every later attempt to correct it
tuples.evidence_lens: printed herbals and the botanical correspondence of the describing naturalists

tuples.episode_object: a sack of seed carried on a ship between two colonial coasts
tuples.time_place_scope: a passage from the Atlantic toward the Indian ocean in the 1500s
tuples.mechanism: traders carry seed as provisions and as goods, so dispersal follows shipping routes rather than any deliberate introduction
tuples.evidence_lens: ship stores accounts and the early botanical records of coastal introductions

tuples.episode_object: a market sample of red powder found brightened with a lead compound
tuples.time_place_scope: a European market town in the inspecting years of the 1800s
tuples.mechanism: colour sells a powder, so cheap mineral pigments are added and public analysis becomes the only defence against poisoning

tuples.episode_object: a wooden pestle turning in a stone mortar drawn by a yoked bullock
tuples.time_place_scope: an Indian village oil mill in the working years of the 1800s
tuples.mechanism: slow cold pressing yields an aromatic oil and a solid cake, so a village mill produces a food and a feed at once
tuples.evidence_lens: village mill account books and the agricultural surveys describing oil pressing

tuples.episode_object: a shallow clay lamp filled with pale oil and a twisted wick
tuples.time_place_scope: a Mediterranean household in the centuries before the 200s
tuples.mechanism: the oil burns cleanly and is used for light and for the body, so an oilseed is grown for purposes far beyond the kitchen
tuples.evidence_lens: excavated lamps and residues and the surviving household and temple accounts

tuples.episode_object: a merchant's sealed jar of oil listed on an overland caravan account
tuples.time_place_scope: a route between Mesopotamia and the Levant in the centuries of the 1000s
tuples.mechanism: oil is dense in value and keeps well, so it travels far inland where the bulky seed itself could not pay the carriage

tuples.episode_object: a marble slab where cooked sugar and ground seed paste are pulled
tuples.time_place_scope: an eastern Mediterranean confectioner's workshop in the 1800s
tuples.mechanism: ground seed paste and sugar make a keeping sweet, so confectionery becomes one of the seed's largest single uses
tuples.evidence_lens: confectioners' recipe books and the workshop production and sale records

tuples.episode_object: a temple offering tray of seed set out beside grain and oil
tuples.time_place_scope: a south Asian temple in the offering seasons of the 1600s
tuples.mechanism: the seed is used in rites for the dead and for the seasons, so ritual demand runs steadily beside any culinary demand
tuples.evidence_lens: temple endowment records and the ritual manuals describing offerings and supplies

tuples.episode_object: a rotating drum where soaked seed is rubbed to loosen its coat
tuples.time_place_scope: an eastern Mediterranean processing works in the 1900s
tuples.mechanism: removing the coat gives a white seed and a milder paste, so a mechanical step creates a distinct and dearer product
tuples.evidence_lens: works process records and the published grade standards for hulled seed

tuples.episode_object: a baker's tray of loaves rolled in seed before they enter the oven
tuples.time_place_scope: an eastern Mediterranean bakery in the working mornings of the 1800s
tuples.mechanism: the seed toasts on a crust and adds oil and aroma, so baking consumes whole seed in a form the oil trade never touches
tuples.evidence_lens: bakery account books and the printed regional recipe collections of the period

tuples.episode_object: a colonial planting report on seed sown across a cleared district
tuples.time_place_scope: an east African district in the 1900s, where export policy spread sesame across cleared land
tuples.mechanism: a drought-tolerant crop is promoted for export by an administration, so cultivation spreads by policy rather than demand
tuples.evidence_lens: colonial agricultural reports and the district planting and export records

tuples.episode_object: a seized sample of oil found blended with a cheaper pressed oil
tuples.time_place_scope: a European inspection office in the 1900s
tuples.mechanism: oils are hard to tell apart once refined, so chemical tests for characteristic components become the inspector's method
tuples.evidence_lens: public analyst reports and the published analytical methods for edible oils

tuples.episode_object: a sample dish of seed weighed and tested for its oil content
tuples.time_place_scope: an exporting port laboratory in the 1900s
tuples.mechanism: buyers pay for oil rather than for seed, so a laboratory figure rather than appearance settles a consignment's price
tuples.evidence_lens: published grading standards and the port laboratory testing certificates

tuples.episode_object: a trial plot of numbered lines whose capsules stay closed when ripe
tuples.time_place_scope: an agricultural research station in the 1900s
tuples.mechanism: breeding for capsules that do not shatter allows machine harvest, so a hand-picked crop becomes mechanically possible
tuples.evidence_lens: research station breeding records and the published variety release descriptions

tuples.episode_object: a printed label listing the seed among declared allergenic ingredients
tuples.time_place_scope: a European labelling office in the defining years of the 2000s
tuples.mechanism: a common allergen must be declared wherever it appears, so labelling law reaches into every product that uses the seed
tuples.evidence_lens: labelling regulations and the trade association guidance issued to manufacturers

tuples.episode_object: a village buying post scale weighing bags brought in by smallholders
tuples.time_place_scope: an east African district in the 1900s, where a village buying post weighed smallholders’ sesame
tuples.mechanism: the crop is grown on very small plots for cash, so the buying post rather than an estate decides a family's income
tuples.evidence_lens: cooperative buying records and the agricultural census returns of smallholdings

tuples.episode_object: a stack of pressed cake blocks carried out to a cattle shed
tuples.time_place_scope: an Indian village mill yard in the 1900s
tuples.mechanism: the residue is a valuable protein feed, so a mill's economics rest on the cake almost as much as on the oil itself

tuples.episode_object: a sealed tin of oil stored away from light upon a cool shelf
tuples.time_place_scope: a south Asian household store room in the 1900s
tuples.mechanism: an unrefined oil turns rancid in warmth and light, so storage practice decides how long a household's pressing lasts
tuples.evidence_lens: household manuals and the agricultural station studies of oil storage

tuples.episode_object: an apothecary jar of oil kept for making ointments and liniments
tuples.time_place_scope: a south Asian dispensing practice in the 1600s
tuples.mechanism: the oil carries other medicines into the skin, so pharmacy uses it as a base and buys it quite apart from any food trade
tuples.evidence_lens: medical treatises of the tradition and the practitioners' preparation notebooks

tuples.episode_object: a laboratory report screening a container for chemical residues
tuples.time_place_scope: a European importing port laboratory in the 2000s
tuples.mechanism: importing countries test consignments for contamination, and a failed test can close a whole country's export trade
tuples.evidence_lens: port inspection laboratory reports and the published import control requirements

tuples.episode_object: a customs entry classing whole seed apart from its pressed oil
tuples.time_place_scope: a European customs house on a routine clearing day in the 1900s
tuples.mechanism: seed and oil carry different duties, so where pressing takes place is decided by a difference in tariff schedules
tuples.evidence_lens: customs classification records and the tariff rulings published on oilseed goods

tuples.episode_object: a trench of straight side roots laid slanting and covered with soil
tuples.time_place_scope: a central European market garden at the planting season of the 1800s
tuples.mechanism: the plant is grown from cuttings of its own side roots, so each year's planting stock comes from the previous crop
tuples.evidence_lens: market garden accounts and the agricultural treatises on root cultivation

tuples.episode_object: a straw-lined clamp of lifted roots covered with earth in a yard

tuples.mechanism: the root keeps in cold damp earth but not in a warm shed, so storage decides whether a crop sells through the winter
tuples.evidence_lens: market garden records and the printed treatises on vegetable storage

tuples.episode_object: a grating board and a cloth held over the face at a kitchen table
tuples.time_place_scope: a central European kitchen in the working years of the 1700s
tuples.mechanism: the heat appears only when cells are broken, so the sharpness is created at the moment of grating and fades in hours
tuples.evidence_lens: household receipt manuscripts and the later chemical studies of the reaction

tuples.episode_object: a poultice of grated root spread on cloth for an aching joint
tuples.time_place_scope: a north European household sickroom in the 1600s
tuples.mechanism: the root draws blood to the skin and is eaten against scurvy, so it is a medicine before it is a table condiment
tuples.evidence_lens: printed herbals and the apothecary registers listing the root's preparations

tuples.episode_object: a plant escaped from a garden and grown wild along a field ditch
tuples.time_place_scope: a north European field margin in the 1800s
tuples.mechanism: broken root fragments regrow readily, so the plant naturalises wherever it is cultivated and becomes hard to remove
tuples.evidence_lens: botanical survey records and the agricultural reports on troublesome weeds

tuples.episode_object: a small dish of grated root in cream set beside a joint of beef

tuples.mechanism: a sharp cold sauce is paired with rich roasted meat, so a table custom fixes when the root is eaten and with what
tuples.evidence_lens: printed cookery books and the household kitchen accounts of great houses

tuples.episode_object: a plate of bitter roots set among the dishes of a spring festival meal
tuples.time_place_scope: a central European Jewish household in the 1800s
tuples.mechanism: a sharp root serves as the bitter herb where others will not grow, so a religious requirement shapes a food supply
tuples.evidence_lens: religious dietary texts and the household provisioning accounts kept for festivals

tuples.episode_object: a jar of sauce found bulked with grated turnip and white starch
tuples.time_place_scope: a British market town in the inspecting years of the 1850s
tuples.mechanism: a pale grated root is easily imitated, so public analysis and later a legal definition are what protect the buyer
tuples.evidence_lens: public analyst reports and the composition standards later published for the sauce

tuples.episode_object: a filling line of small jars sealed with vinegar and a little salt
tuples.time_place_scope: a north American works in the working shifts of the 1900s
tuples.mechanism: acid holds the pungency and prevents spoilage, so bottling makes a fleeting sharpness into a lasting shelf product
tuples.evidence_lens: works process records and the trade press reporting on the packaged sauce trade

tuples.episode_object: a contract with growers specifying an acreage and a delivery weight
tuples.time_place_scope: a north American farming district in the 1900s, where contracts linked root growers to year-round works supply
tuples.mechanism: a works needs roots all year and growers need a certain buyer, so contract farming rather than a market links the two
tuples.evidence_lens: manufacturers' grower contracts and the farm cropping and delivery records

tuples.episode_object: a grating room with extraction fans and workers in eye protection
tuples.time_place_scope: a processing works in north America in the 1900s
tuples.mechanism: the released vapour is punishing to work in, so ventilation and protective equipment shape how a factory is built
tuples.evidence_lens: works plant records and the factory inspection and safety reports of the period

tuples.episode_object: a herbal page giving the root a name that means neither horse nor radish
tuples.time_place_scope: a European printing town in the naming years of the 1500s
tuples.mechanism: a folk name is built from mishearing and comparison, so a plant carries a name that describes nothing about it

tuples.episode_object: a brewer's note adding grated root to a cask of country ale
tuples.time_place_scope: an English farm brewhouse in the brewing weeks of the 1600s
tuples.mechanism: sharp roots and herbs flavour and preserve small country beers, so a condiment plant enters a different trade entirely
tuples.evidence_lens: household receipt manuscripts and the printed brewing manuals of the period

tuples.episode_object: a sorting bench separating straight thick roots from thin crooked ones
tuples.time_place_scope: a central European packing shed in the 1900s
tuples.mechanism: straight thick roots grate cleanly and sell for more, so grading after lifting decides which market a crop can reach
tuples.evidence_lens: published grade standards and the packing shed sorting and inspection records

tuples.episode_object: a cold store room holding crated roots at a steady low temperature
tuples.time_place_scope: a north American works yard in the 1900s
tuples.mechanism: refrigerated storage lets a seasonal root be processed all year, so cold rather than any farming change ends the season
tuples.evidence_lens: works storage records and the refrigeration engineering reports of the period

tuples.episode_object: a veterinary manual page recommending the root for a horse's chest
tuples.time_place_scope: a north European farm through the working year of the 1800s
tuples.mechanism: the same sharpness used on people is used on animals, so a garden plant sits in a kitchen and in a stable alike
tuples.evidence_lens: printed veterinary manuals and the farm purchase and treatment records

tuples.episode_object: an immigrant family's small works grating roots for a city market
tuples.time_place_scope: a north American city in the 1900s, where an immigrant family grated roots for a city market
tuples.mechanism: migrants bring a taste and a trade together, so a regional European condiment becomes a local American manufacture
tuples.evidence_lens: immigrant community records and the local business and licensing registers

tuples.episode_object: a standards notice naming a minimum root content for a bottled sauce
tuples.time_place_scope: a north American regulatory office in the 1900s, where a root-content standard governed bottled sauce
tuples.mechanism: a legal minimum tells a buyer what is in a jar, so a word on a label becomes a measurable and enforceable quantity
tuples.evidence_lens: published standards of identity and the trade association guidance to producers

tuples.episode_object: a laboratory flask measuring the pungent compound released on grating
tuples.time_place_scope: a European chemical laboratory in the 1800s
tuples.mechanism: an enzyme releases a volatile compound when tissue is broken, so a kitchen observation is explained as a reaction
tuples.evidence_lens: published chemical papers and the laboratory notebooks describing the reaction

tuples.episode_object: a market gardener's ledger comparing root prices across three winters
tuples.time_place_scope: a central European growing district in the 1900s
tuples.mechanism: a bulky root is costly to carry and quick to lose its heat, so price is set by distance from a works as much as by yield
tuples.evidence_lens: market garden ledgers and the district market and price records of the period

tuples.episode_object: a terraced bed of graded gravel with cold water running through it
tuples.time_place_scope: a mountain valley in central Japan in the growing years of the 1700s
tuples.mechanism: the plant needs constantly moving cold water at its roots, so cultivation is really a matter of building and keeping a stream
tuples.evidence_lens: domain agricultural records and the later technical surveys of the growing beds

tuples.episode_object: a planting crew standing in shallow water setting seedlings by hand
tuples.time_place_scope: a Japanese mountain stream bed in the planting weeks of the 1900s
tuples.mechanism: every plant is set and lifted by hand in cold water, so labour rather than land is what limits how much can be grown
tuples.evidence_lens: grower association records and the agricultural extension reports on labour

tuples.episode_object: a lifted rhizome showing two years of growth marked in leaf scars
tuples.time_place_scope: a Japanese mountain farm in the harvest months of the 1900s
tuples.mechanism: the rhizome takes a year or two to reach saleable size, so a grower's income is locked up in the beds for a long time
tuples.evidence_lens: farm production records and the agricultural station studies of growth and yield

tuples.episode_object: a small board covered with dried shark skin used as a grating surface
tuples.time_place_scope: a Japanese kitchen in the working years of the 1800s
tuples.mechanism: a very fine grating surface breaks the cells gently, so the utensil is judged to change the taste as much as the plant
tuples.evidence_lens: trade catalogues of kitchen utensils and the printed cookery manuals of the period

tuples.episode_object: a small mound of grated paste made moments before it is served
tuples.time_place_scope: a Japanese eating house in the working evenings of the 1800s
tuples.mechanism: the pungency appears on grating and fades within minutes, so preparation must happen at the table and not in a kitchen
tuples.evidence_lens: printed cookery manuals and the later chemical studies of the volatile compounds

tuples.episode_object: a counter tray of sliced raw fish with a smear of green paste beside it
tuples.time_place_scope: a Japanese city eating stall in the 1800s
tuples.mechanism: the paste is served with raw fish for taste and for a belief in its safety, so a condiment is bound to one way of eating
tuples.evidence_lens: printed cookery manuals and the ethnographic surveys of urban food stalls

tuples.episode_object: a domain record noting a mountain crop reserved for a ruling household
tuples.time_place_scope: a central Japanese domain in the recording years of the 1600s
tuples.mechanism: a scarce mountain plant is claimed by a lord and encouraged, so patronage rather than trade begins the whole industry
tuples.evidence_lens: domain administrative records and the local histories of the growing districts

tuples.episode_object: a shaded field of plants grown in cool damp soil rather than in water
tuples.time_place_scope: a Japanese upland farm in the 1900s, where shade-grown roots were graded by their cultivation method
tuples.mechanism: growing in soil is faster and cheaper but gives a coarser root, so two methods produce two grades from one plant
tuples.evidence_lens: agricultural station comparative trials and the grower association grade records

tuples.episode_object: a tin of green powder made from a European root with added colouring
tuples.time_place_scope: a food works in east Asia in the 1900s, where coloured European root was made into a cheaper paste
tuples.mechanism: a cheap sharp root coloured green stands in for a costly one, so most of what is eaten under the name is another plant
tuples.evidence_lens: works production records and the composition and labelling standards of the period

tuples.episode_object: a printed label stating the percentage of the true rhizome present
tuples.time_place_scope: a Japanese labelling office in the 1900s, where labels stated the percentage of true rhizome
tuples.mechanism: law is written to say how much of the named plant a product must hold, so a word on a tube becomes a measurable claim
tuples.evidence_lens: labelling regulations and the trade association guidance issued to producers

tuples.episode_object: a trial planting laid in a cold spring-fed channel far from Japan
tuples.time_place_scope: a temperate upland district in the trialling years of the 1990s
tuples.mechanism: the water requirements are hard to reproduce, so attempts to grow the crop abroad succeed only where cold springs run
tuples.evidence_lens: agricultural research station trial reports and the growers' association records

tuples.episode_object: a thermometer and a flow gauge fixed at the head of a growing bed
tuples.time_place_scope: a Japanese mountain farm through the cold seasons of the 1900s
tuples.mechanism: temperature and flow decide whether a bed thrives or rots, so measurement of water is the central skill of cultivation
tuples.evidence_lens: farm management records and the agricultural station studies of water conditions

tuples.episode_object: a bed emptied and its gravel washed after a spreading root disease
tuples.time_place_scope: a Japanese growing valley in the 1900s, where washed gravel checked disease in successive crops
tuples.mechanism: disease builds in the beds over successive crops, so the gravel must be cleaned and rested as carefully as any soil
tuples.evidence_lens: plant health inspection records and the agricultural station disease survey reports

tuples.episode_object: a grower's account showing two years of costs against one harvest
tuples.time_place_scope: a Japanese mountain farm through the cold seasons of the 1900s
tuples.mechanism: a long crop cycle and heavy hand labour make the price high, so scarcity here is a matter of time rather than of land
tuples.evidence_lens: farm account books and the district agricultural cost and price surveys

tuples.episode_object: a laboratory rack of plantlets raised in sterile jars of nutrient gel
tuples.time_place_scope: a Japanese research station in the 1980s
tuples.mechanism: raising disease-free plantlets in a laboratory secures the planting stock, so propagation moves indoors before planting
tuples.evidence_lens: research station technical reports and the plant health certification records

tuples.episode_object: a crock of leaves and stems pickled in brewing lees on a farm shelf
tuples.time_place_scope: a Japanese mountain household in the preserving weeks of the 1900s
tuples.mechanism: the parts that cannot be sold as rhizome are pickled and eaten, so nothing of a costly crop is allowed to be wasted
tuples.evidence_lens: household recipe collections and the regional food surveys of the growing districts

tuples.episode_object: a filling machine sealing green paste into small collapsible tubes
tuples.time_place_scope: a Japanese food works through the packing shifts of the 1900s
tuples.mechanism: a paste that loses pungency in minutes is stabilised and sealed, so packaging preserves a quality it also somewhat changes
tuples.evidence_lens: works process records and the packaging machinery catalogues of the period

tuples.episode_object: a physician's note recommending the grated root against food poisoning
tuples.time_place_scope: a Japanese medical practice in the 1700s
tuples.mechanism: the plant is prescribed as a preservative and a remedy, so medical belief and culinary practice reinforce one another
tuples.evidence_lens: medical treatises of the tradition and the practitioners' preparation notebooks

tuples.episode_object: a visitor path and a sign board built beside a working growing bed
tuples.time_place_scope: a Japanese mountain valley in the visiting seasons of the 1900s
tuples.mechanism: the beds themselves become a place people travel to see, so a farm earns from visitors as well as from the crop it lifts
tuples.evidence_lens: local tourism records and the municipal accounts of visitor facilities

tuples.episode_object: an association register of growers permitted to use a valley's name
tuples.time_place_scope: a Japanese producing district in the 1900s, where grower registration protected a valley name
tuples.mechanism: a district records who may sell under its name, so geography is used to separate a scarce crop from its substitutes
tuples.evidence_lens: producers' association registers and the district inspection and audit records

tuples.episode_object: a trench dug two spades deep to lift a long branching root
tuples.time_place_scope: a Yorkshire garden field at the harvest of the 1600s
tuples.mechanism: the root runs deep and takes several years to grow, so lifting it is heavy work done only once in a long rotation
tuples.evidence_lens: estate and town garden records and the agricultural treatises on root crops

tuples.episode_object: a bundle of wild-dug roots tied and stacked beside a river landing
tuples.time_place_scope: a Central Asian river valley in the collecting seasons of the 1800s
tuples.mechanism: the plant grows wild along rivers in great quantity, so most of the world supply is gathered rather than cultivated
tuples.evidence_lens: trade reports and the botanical and agricultural surveys of the collecting districts

tuples.episode_object: a boiling pan reducing root liquor down to a stiff black paste
tuples.time_place_scope: a Mediterranean extract works in the working years of the 1800s
tuples.mechanism: boiling and evaporating gives a hard block that keeps and travels, so extract rather than root becomes the traded good
tuples.evidence_lens: works production records and the trade descriptions of block extract grades

tuples.episode_object: a monastic garden plot recorded as planted with the deep root
tuples.time_place_scope: an English monastic town in the growing years of the 1500s
tuples.mechanism: religious houses grow medicinal plants and pass them to a town, so a garden founds an industry that outlives it
tuples.evidence_lens: monastic garden and infirmary records and the later borough trade registers

tuples.episode_object: an apothecary jar of black extract weighed for a cough preparation
tuples.time_place_scope: a dispensing shop in a north European town in the 1600s
tuples.mechanism: the root soothes the throat and masks bitter medicines, so pharmacy uses it both as a remedy and as a flavouring
tuples.evidence_lens: apothecary registers and the printed pharmacopoeia entries for the preparation

tuples.episode_object: a stamped disc of black paste pressed with a small carved seal
tuples.time_place_scope: a Yorkshire sweet workshop in the working years of the 1800s
tuples.mechanism: a medicinal lozenge becomes a stamped sweet, so a town's pharmacy trade turns into a confectionery trade in a century
tuples.evidence_lens: workshop production records and the borough trade and business registers

tuples.episode_object: a casing works vat where cut tobacco leaf is sprayed with a dark liquor
tuples.time_place_scope: a north American tobacco works in the 1900s
tuples.mechanism: the extract sweetens and holds moisture in cut tobacco, so a manufacturing industry rather than food buys most of it
tuples.evidence_lens: works production records and the trade journals of the tobacco manufacturing trade

tuples.episode_object: a brewer's store of extract weighed against a dark beer recipe
tuples.time_place_scope: an English brewhouse in the working years of the 1800s
tuples.mechanism: the extract deepens colour and sweetness in strong dark beers, so a root enters brewing as a cheap and lawful addition
tuples.evidence_lens: brewery recipe books and the excise records of ingredients entered for use

tuples.episode_object: a sample of extract found bulked with starch and with molasses
tuples.time_place_scope: a European inspection office in the 1900s
tuples.mechanism: a dark sticky paste hides additions easily, so testing for the characteristic sweet compound becomes the standard method
tuples.evidence_lens: public analyst reports and the published analytical methods for the extract

tuples.episode_object: an importer's bale of cleaned root landed from an eastern port
tuples.time_place_scope: a north European port in the trading years of the 1800s
tuples.mechanism: a bulky low-value root travels only where freight is cheap, so importers site their extraction works close to the docks
tuples.evidence_lens: port import registers and the works purchase and processing records

tuples.episode_object: a laboratory flask isolating the compound that makes the root sweet
tuples.time_place_scope: a European chemical laboratory in the 1800s
tuples.mechanism: a single compound proves many times sweeter than sugar, so chemistry explains a taste that had long been in use
tuples.evidence_lens: published chemical papers and the laboratory notebooks describing the isolation

tuples.episode_object: a regulatory notice setting a daily limit for the sweet compound
tuples.time_place_scope: a European regulatory office in the defining years of the 1990s
tuples.mechanism: the same compound raises blood pressure when eaten in quantity, so a traditional sweet is given a published limit
tuples.evidence_lens: published food safety opinions and the regulatory guidance issued to producers

tuples.episode_object: a hand press stamping a town's arms into soft black discs
tuples.time_place_scope: a Yorkshire workshop in the working years of the 1800s
tuples.mechanism: a stamped mark identifies a town's make, so a small regional craft protects itself by an impression rather than by law
tuples.evidence_lens: workshop production records and the local trade and business directories

tuples.episode_object: a battery of extraction vessels percolating milled root with hot water
tuples.time_place_scope: a European extract works through the processing season of the 1900s
tuples.mechanism: continuous percolation replaces boiling in open pans, so extraction moves from a craft process into a chemical plant
tuples.evidence_lens: works plant inventories and the engineering trade descriptions of extraction plant

tuples.episode_object: a shop counter where a lozenge is sold beside a jar of black sweets
tuples.time_place_scope: a British high street on a working afternoon in the 1900s
tuples.mechanism: the same material is medicine in one shop and confectionery in another, so regulation follows the counter not the root
tuples.evidence_lens: pharmacy and confectionery trade registers and the labelling rules of the period

tuples.episode_object: a deep plough drawn by a traction engine across a growing field
tuples.time_place_scope: a Mediterranean growing district in the 1900s
tuples.mechanism: a deep root needs deep cultivation and deep lifting, so mechanisation reaches the crop through ploughing before harvest
tuples.evidence_lens: agricultural machinery records and the estate cultivation and cropping accounts

tuples.episode_object: a washing trough where lifted roots are cleaned and cut to length
tuples.time_place_scope: a Middle Eastern collecting yard in the 1900s
tuples.mechanism: soil and bark lower the value of a consignment, so washing and trimming before sale is what sets the grade of a lot
tuples.evidence_lens: published grade standards and the collecting yard sorting and inspection records

tuples.episode_object: a works order for extract to be used in a foam-making preparation
tuples.time_place_scope: an industrial chemical works in the 1900s
tuples.mechanism: the root's saponins make a stable foam, so an extract is bought for industrial uses far outside food or medicine
tuples.evidence_lens: works purchase records and the technical trade journals describing the applications

tuples.episode_object: a state export licence issued for a consignment of cleaned root
tuples.time_place_scope: a Middle Eastern port in the 1900s, where cleaned licorice root required an export licence
tuples.mechanism: a wild crop of national importance is licensed for export, so collection and shipment are administered as a public resource
tuples.evidence_lens: export licensing files and the state trade and forestry administration records

tuples.episode_object: a heritage register entry naming a town's sweet among protected foods
tuples.time_place_scope: a British registering office in the 2000s
tuples.mechanism: a town's declining craft is recorded and protected by name, so listing preserves what the market no longer sustains
tuples.evidence_lens: protected designation registers and the local trade association application files

compatibility_rules: Pair only with the sleep history compilation formula; these chapters assume no hooks, no host presence, and no narrative arc running across a video.
Build each chapter from one subject and one coverage tuple, and never combine two subjects into a single chapter.
Use at most twenty chapters from this pack in one compilation, and do not take the same subject twice within a single video.
evidence_expectations: Lean on the source types named in each tuple's evidence lens, and describe them as classes of record rather than citing specific titles, authors, or archives.
State a period as a decade or a century and a place as a region or a kind of settlement; do not invent exact dates, quantities, or prices.
Where the record is thin or disputed, say so plainly in one calm sentence and move on rather than filling the gap with invention.
Keep the process at the centre of the account: describe how a thing was grown, made, carried, taxed, or judged, and let the named sources support that description.
